Article Title: 'Mortgaging self-respect': Raut takes aim at Sharad Pawar's NCP over delimitation bill
Article Text:
'People won't tolerate it': Raut warns NCP (SP) against backing delimitation bill

Raut questions NCP (SP)'s stand

Calls delimitation a threat to democracy

What the proposed bill seeks to do

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut on Saturday accused the BJP of engineering a split in the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) and the Pawar family, saying any move by the NCP (SP) to support the Centre's proposed delimitation bill would amount to mortgaging its self-respect.Raut said the BJP had divided the NCP and the Pawar family, and alleged that aligning with the saffron party would mean surrendering one's self-respect.Speaking to reporters, the Rajya Sabha MP said the NCP (SP) should reconsider its reported decision to back the legislation, calling it an unfortunate and unilateral move that would not go down well with people in Maharashtra."If you are taking unilateral decisions and backing the government on the bill, then the people of Maharashtra will not tolerate it," he was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.Questioning the party's reported willingness to support the bill, Raut said its eight MPs had won the Lok Sabha election as part of the Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA), and not with the BJP's support."Your eight MPs won as Maha Vikas Aghadi. BJP did not help them win," he said.He also asked the NCP (SP) to apologise to leaders such as Anil Deshmukh and Nawab Malik, who, he claimed, had faced jail while fighting the BJP.Raut said backing the legislation would be contrary to the ideology of the NCP (SP) and Maharashtra's political legacy.He added that parties should not invoke the ideals of Mahatma Phule, Shahu Maharaj and Dr BR Ambedkar while supporting the bill.Raut alleged that the proposed delimitation exercise was intended to weaken democratic institutions and strengthen the BJP ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections."By raising the number of 543 to 806 MPs and then doing delimitation as per your whim...this is snatching people's rights forever. This is a conspiracy of the BJP," he said.He also accused the BJP of not winning all its elections on merit, alleging that it had misled voters in 2014 and resorted to an EVM "scam" and "vote chori and seat chori" in 2024. He claimed the government was now pushing delimitation after the Opposition had exposed these alleged irregularities."This (the delimitation process) is detrimental for the country and its federal system," Raut said, warning that the passage of the bill would leave no room for the Constitution, freedom or democracy.The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared a fresh delimitation-linked women's reservation bill ahead of the special Parliament sitting beginning November 30.The proposal seeks to increase Lok Sabha seats by 50 per cent across all states, taking the House's proposed upper limit to 850 from the existing 543. The increased seats would be redrawn using the 2011 Census, while each state's percentage share of parliamentary representation would remain unchanged, sources said.The government is seeking support from parties including the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the NCP (SP) to secure the numbers needed to pass the legislation.The BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) could secure 319 votes with the support of 20 Trinamool Congress rebels and the lone Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) MP, whose party returned to the NDA on November 24.The tally could increase to 353 if the DMK's 22 MPs, the NCP (SP)'s eight MPs and the YSR Congress Party's four MPs also support the bill.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut accuses the BJP of engineering a split in the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) and the Pawar family. Raut says any move by the NCP (SP) to support the Centre's proposed delimitation bill would amount to mortgaging its self-respect.

Article Title: ‘Today one Deepam, tomorrow temples?’ Vaishnaw slams TVK govt over Thiruparankundram Deepam row
Article Text:
Vaishnaw slams TVK government over Thiruparankundram Deepam row in Tamil Nadu

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Thursday launched a sharp attack on the Tamil Nadu government over the Thiruparankundram Karthigai Deepam row, accusing it of hurting the religious sentiments of millions. He also cautioned the state government against attempts to restrict temple traditions and religious practices.Addressing a Constitution Day event organised by the BJP in Chennai, Vaishnaw further targeted the Congress, accusing it of placing family interests above constitutional values.Referring to the dispute over lighting the ceremonial lamp at the Deepathoon stone pillar, Vaishnaw questioned the Vijay government's position and warned that restrictions on religious practices could have wider implications."Tamil Nadu is intact. Stopping one deepam, you have stopped, you have hurt, you have destroyed and disturbed the emotions of millions of people. What will happen? Today you have stopped one deepam, tomorrow you will say that nobody can go to a temple? They'll shut down the temples. Is that what they want?" he said, according to news agency PTI.Vaishnaw also said, "True respect for the Constitution means safeguarding religious freedom and taking pride in our culture, Lord Muruga, and our ancient heritage."The remarks came amid continuing tensions over the annual Karthigai Deepam ceremony. Maha Deepam was lit above the Uchi Pillayar temple at Thiruparankundram Hills amid heavy security, but no lamp was lit at the disputed Deepathoon pillar. A team of priests associated with the Subramaniaswamy temple performed the ceremony at the usual location.The dispute escalated after a scuffle broke out between members of Hindu organisations and police. Several people, including BJP leaders and members of Hindu outfits, were detained amid restrictions imposed by authorities over law-and-order concerns.The matter is also before the Supreme Court. On Thursday, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said contempt petitions and other applications concerning the non-lighting of the lamp at Deepathoon would be listed on November 27."Everything will be listed tomorrow," the bench said. The Tamil Nadu government had apologised to the court on Wednesday over the incident, blaming the temple authorities. The apex court had earlier declined to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings.Vaishnaw also criticised the Congress over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and electronic voting machines (EVMs), alleging that the party questioned electoral processes selectively."Congress wants to just blame SIR for their own failures. And they will keep failing like this. Because for them, it is not the Constitution, it is the family," he said.Turning to railway development, the minister claimed that Tamil Nadu had acquired only 1,253 hectares, or 24 per cent, of the approximately 4,800 hectares required for railway projects.He urged the state government to expedite land acquisition, assuring that the Centre would provide the necessary funds. Vaishnaw also highlighted the redevelopment of 77 railway stations in Tamil Nadu and discussed proposed high-speed rail connectivity between Chennai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.The Supreme Court's scheduled hearing on Saturday is expected to bring further clarity to the contempt petitions and applications.
Article Summary: Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw slams TVK government over Thiruparankundram Deepam row. Accuses Tamil Nadu government of hurting religious sentiments of millions. Warns against attempts to restrict temple traditions and religious practices. Further criticised Congress for placing family interests above constitutional values.

Article Title: 'Fake news': CJP's Ranka threatens legal action over claim leaders fled Nagpur rally venue after Look Out Circulars issued
Article Text:
CJP’s Ranka accuses news agency of ‘fake news’ over leaders’ rally exit amid LOC row

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka has threatened legal action against news agency IANS, accusing it of spreading fake news over a video posted on X. The agency had claimed that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and his associates left a venue after receiving information about a Look Out Circular (LOC), while avoiding media cameras.In its post, IANS wrote: "As soon as they received information about the Look Out Notice, CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke and his associates began leaving the spot while avoiding media cameras. They left before Actor Prakash Raj could speak."Responding to the post, Ranka said the agency had published an inaccurate account of the events and warned it to expect a legal notice."Dear IANS, Instead of posting from the IT cell account, you accidentally posted from your official id. You might now wait for a legal notice for spreading fake news, since there are videos of Prakash Sir addressing the audience and all of us comfortably leaving the venue with police around," he wrote on X.The video posted by IANS showed reporters following vehicles carrying CJP leaders as they left the venue. It later showed actor Prakash Raj being escorted by a police official as media personnel gathered around him. However, the footage does not establish the context claimed in the agency's post.The exchange came amid a protest organised by the CJP in Nagpur on Thursday, where Dipke and other party leaders addressed a rally titled 'Save Democracy, Save Constitution' at Samvidhan Chowk on Constitution Day.Addressing the gathering, Dipke accused the BJP-led Centre of undermining the Constitution and alleged that institutions across the country had been hijacked."The government is acting against the Constitution. Not a single institution is left that has not been hijacked," he said.Referring to the LOC issued against him by Mumbai Police, Dipke challenged the authorities to arrest him."There is a lookout notice against me by the Mumbai Police. There is police bandobast here and they are looking for me. Where is Abhijeet Dipke? I am here in Samvidhan Chowk. What will you do? Arrest me. I have been in jail twice. Don't show me the fear of jail," he said.Ranka, meanwhile, said the party was preparing to expand its activities beyond protests in major cities. "We will go to every village, interact with people and give a voice to the youth," he said.Mumbai Police have issued LOCs against Dipke, Ranka and CJP leader Saurav Das in connection with an FIR over an alleged unauthorised protest at Shivaji Park on Gandhi Jayanti. Police said the circulars were issued to prevent the leaders from leaving the country while the investigation was underway.Das was stopped at the airport on November 23 while attempting to travel to the United Kingdom for an event at Oxford University. He has challenged the LOC before the Delhi High Court.
Article Summary: CJP co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka has threatened legal action against news agency IANS. Ranka accused IANS of spreading fake news over a video posted on X. The agency had claimed that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and his associates left a venue after receiving information about a Look Out Circular.

Article Title: 'Money-minded manifesto': Mayawati slams Akhilesh Yadav's SP ahead of 2027 UP polls
Article Text:
Mayawati slams Akhilesh Yadav

NEW DELHI: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Samajwadi Party (SP) over its recently released 'Manifesto of the People's Will' for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, dismissing it as "little more than empty rhetoric" and a "money-minded manifesto" rather than a genuine commitment to public welfare.In a post on X, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister said the SP's manifesto was similar to its 'PDA' (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) initiative and reflected the saying "all show, no substance".Mayawati alleged that the SP had consistently followed a "narrow-minded, casteist and pro-big business" approach that went against the interests, welfare, dignity and security of poor people, Dalits, backward classes, Muslims and other sections of society.She also cited the SP's alleged preference for a wealthy businessperson over supporting the PDA in the recent biennial Rajya Sabha elections from Uttar Pradesh as an example of its political approach.Questioning whether such policies could address the state's problems, including poverty, unemployment, backwardness and migration, Mayawati said the SP's manifesto was more concerned with financial interests than public welfare.She further alleged that the party would continue to field wealthy candidates and strongmen rather than people committed to public and social interests.Defending her party's record, Mayawati said the principles of "work for every hand" and "the rule of law through the law" belonged to the BSP and had been implemented during all four of its governments in Uttar Pradesh.She also accused the SP of having a record of opposing reservations for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs), and of contributing to caste-based hostility and riots in the state.In her post, she described the SP's promises and declarations as "electoral deception and trickery", urging voters to remain cautious.Mayawati pitches BSP as authentic Ambedkarite partyWith Assembly elections approaching in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Punjab, Mayawati called for strengthening the BSP, describing it as the only authentic Ambedkarite party capable of translating the ideals of the Constitution into reality.“Given that the general assembly elections—particularly in Uttar Pradesh, as well as in Uttarakhand and Punjab—are fast approaching, it is imperative to effectively translate the noble intent of Babasaheb Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar’s Constitution into reality. This cannot be achieved through the mindset or working culture of narrow-minded, feudal, or casteist parties; rather, it can only be realised through the advancement of the BSP—the sole, authentic Ambedkarite party—which guarantees the welfare of all sections of society and ensures the safety of their lives, property, and religious beliefs, while fostering the upliftment of the 'Bahujan Samaj’," she said.Mayawati said the BSP aimed to establish the rule of law in Uttar Pradesh and promote a governance model centred on public welfare, social well-being and development.“So that an 'iron rule of law' can be established here in UP, along with a governance model rooted in the principle of 'the welfare and happiness of all '—prioritising public interest, social well-being, and development. This would enable all sections of society—currently plagued by poverty, unemployment, backwardness, and the distress of forced migration—to lead a prosperous life filled with peace and happiness,” she added.The BSP, which governed Uttar Pradesh from 2007 to 2012, was reduced to a single seat in the 2022 Assembly elections despite securing more than 13 per cent of the vote share.The party failed to win a single seat in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.SP-Congress seat-sharing talks continueMeanwhile, the SP is preparing to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in alliance with the Congress. The two INDIA bloc partners are continuing negotiations over seat-sharing, with the SP having offered 26 seats to the Congress in the initial round of discussions.The Congress, however, has sought 120 seats and is unwilling to accept a lower number, according to sources.The SP is seeking to return to power after consecutive defeats in the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections. It won 111 seats in the 2022 polls.
Article Summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati slams Samajwadi Party (SP) over its recently released 'Manifesto of the People's Will' for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Former Uttar Pradesh chief minister said the SP's manifesto was similar to its 'PDA' (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) initiative.

Article Title: 'BJP's biggest political mistake': Akhilesh slams Delimitation Bill ahead of Parliament's special session - How numbers stack up
Article Text:
Akhilesh Yadav's remarks came a day after the government announced a special sitting of Parliament from November 30 to December 3.

‘Mischievous PM-HM jodi is lying’

Decoding the delimitation maths.

‘Thackeray is no more, Pawar is unwell’: Shiv Sena (UBT)

How numbers stack up?

Decoding delimitation maths

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Friday attacked the ruling BJP over the proposed delimitation-linked women's reservation bill, saying it would prove to be the party's “biggest political mistake”.“Delimitation will prove to be the biggest political mistake made by the BJP,” Akhilesh said in a post on X.His remarks came a day after the government announced a special sitting of Parliament from November 30 to December 3 to transact “essential” business, amid speculation that it may reintroduce the delimitation-linked women's reservation bill.The proposed legislation seeks to increase the Lok Sabha's strength from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats through delimitation, paving the way for the implementation of 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections.Congress also alleged that the special session had little to do with women's reservation and accused the government of using it to push the delimitation bill.“Yet again, the mischievous PM-HM jodi is lying,” Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said on X.Ramesh pointed out that the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, providing one-third reservation for women, was passed unanimously by Parliament in September 2023.The Congress president had subsequently demanded its immediate implementation, but the law was not notified until 10.40 pm on April 16, 2026, he said.“The Special Session is thus NOT for women's reservation. That is already a law which the PM-HM jodi have put into cold storage for over three years,” Ramesh said.He alleged that the government was convening Parliament to push delimitation and redraw constituencies to benefit the BJP.“And who will be in charge of deciding the geography of constituencies? It will be a thoroughly compromised and brutally exposed CEC, Gyanesh Kumar, who has made a complete mockery of preparation of electoral rolls and destroyed the integrity of the electoral process,” he said.“The executors of Vote Chori on such a gigantic scale are to be given the powers to carry out delimitation and manipulate the nature of constituencies. This is as atrocious as you can get.“This is a desperate move by a nervous and rattled PM who is under siege. It will be countered with firm resolve,” Ramesh added.The Congress has also alleged that the government is hoping to secure a “super-tainted” two-thirds majority to pass the Constitution amendment bill.Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut also opposed the proposed delimitation exercise, alleging that it was a BJP conspiracy to take away people's political power.Sharing a post on X, Raut said, “Today, Shiv Sena chief Balasaheb Thackeray is no longer with us: Sharad Pawar is unwell and in no position to fight or make decisions, otherwise the anti-national Delimitation Bill would never have dared to be brought before Parliament in such a corrupt manner: Delimitation is a BJP conspiracy to strip the people of this country of their power.”“Anyone who supports it is betraying the people of this country… They will be known as the biggest traitors of the 21st century! Therefore, every patriotic, democratic party should reject Delimitation in Parliament. History always remembers the names of traitors; Explanations for betrayal fade into thin air” he added.Meanwhile, the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) is likely to support the delimitation bill, provided it ensures regional balance, party sources told ANI.The Lok Sabha Secretariat said the second part of the eighth session of the 18th Lok Sabha will begin on November 30. The special sitting is expected to conclude on December 3, subject to the exigencies of government business.The sittings will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 but not prorogued.Earlier on Thursday, Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Houses to transact essential government business.The Union Cabinet is also scheduled to meet on Friday and is likely to discuss the delimitation-linked women's reservation legislation, sources said.The developments follow Prime Minister Narendra Modi's remarks on Thursday, accusing an opposition party of blocking the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, in April.In a signed article published in newspapers, PM Modi, “The journey of our Constitution would be incomplete without recognising the remarkable women who helped shape it. But what happened earlier this year should fill our hearts with shame.”“I assure the 'Nari Shakti' of India that no force can prevent us from ensuring that justice is done to them,” he added.The bill was defeated in April after the government failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha. It needs 361 votes in the 543-member House, which currently has 540 members due to three vacancies.The NDA has around 320 MPs and would require additional support from opposition parties to cross the threshold.The government's position has strengthened since the bill's defeat in April, with 26 MPs moving out of the opposition camp.Twenty rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA, while six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.However, the ruling alliance still needs additional votes. The DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (SP), with eight, could play a significant role in the evolving political arithmetic.Opposition parties are also expected to raise their protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, potentially leading to another stormy session.
Article Summary: The proposed legislation seeks to increase the Lok Sabha's strength from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats. It would pave the way for the implementation of 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections. The government announced a special sitting of Parliament from November 30 to December 3.

Article Title: Supreme Court raps TVK government, orders lamp lit at Tamil Nadu site today
Article Text:
The Supreme Court came down heavily on the Tamil Nadu government for not complying with its order

An order of this court is not an invitation to negotiate, warns Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: In a rebuke to the Vijay government, the Supreme Court on Friday initiated contempt proceedings against top officers of Tamil Nadu — its chief secretary, DGP and 11 others — for “wilful” and “deliberate” disobedience of its order on lamp lighting at Deepathoon at the temple of Lord Murugan and acting not on its direction, but seemingly “on the dictates of their political boss”.It directed that lighting would be done on Saturday and, unlike in the previous order where only limited people were allowed to light the lamp, Supreme Court said that now every devotee can light the lamp at the disputed site 50 metres away from the nearby dargah.Holding that the majesty of the court is non-negotiable, Supreme Court also directed CRPF to take over the security of the site from the state police, indicating that the court had lost faith in the state administration to carry out its order. The bench then went on to suspend the board of trustees of Arulmigu Subramania Swamy Temple and appointed former Madras HC judges Justice S Vaidyanathan and Justice V Parthiban as receivers to manage the affairs of the site. The court said that the conduct of all state authorities, including the board of trustees and state police, shocked its conscience.The Supreme Court made it clear that all state authorities must be treated with an iron hand for creating “constitutional chaos” by refusing to comply with its order.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi held that a contempt case is prima facie made out against them and directed them to appear before it on Dec 15 to explain the defiance of the apex court’s directive.The non-compliance stood out against the backdrop of opposition to the lighting of the lamp atop the Deepathoon from Sikandar Badusha Dargah Committee, state government, its Hindu religious and charitable endowments department, Madurai district administration, and the temple board of trustees.An array of political parties — TVK as well as its predecessor in office, DMK, Congress, Left parties — and Muslim outfits have been opposing the move.Expressing its “pain and anguish” at the way in which its order had been undermined, the court indicated that it was left with no option but to deal with an iron hand, or it would lead to constitutional chaos. At the outset of dictating the order, Justice Kumar said, “Alas is the first word that comes to mind.”It said the concept of the rule of law is supreme in a democratic society and cannot be allowed to be weakened, and it is mandatory under Article 14 for all authorities, civil and judicial, in the territory of India to act in aid of the Supreme Court.“An order of this court is not an invitation to negotiate. It binds the state, its officers and every statutory or religious institution functioning under the state’s law until this court itself modifies it. Any attempt to pollute the stream of justice by any person, howsoever high he may be, would not be tolerated… Therefore, when an order of this court is violated, we cannot sit in silos… This is the message which we intend to convey in this order. ”
Article Summary: The Supreme Court initiated contempt proceedings against top officers of Tamil Nadu. The court said that the conduct of all state authorities, including the board of trustees and state police, shocked its conscience.Expressing its “pain and anguish” at the way in which its order had been undermined, the court indicated that it was left with no option but to deal with an iron hand.

Article Title: Deepam lighting at Deepathoon at 5pm, 50 people allowed atop Thiruparankundram hill

Deepam lighting at Deepathoon stone pillar on November 28

THIRUPARANKUNDRAM: The traditional Karthigai Deepam will be lit atop the stone pillar (Deepathoon) on Thiruparankundram hill at 5pm on Saturday, former Meghalaya High Court chief justice S Vaidyanathan said, following the Supreme Court's directive.Justice Vaidyanathan, who arrived in Madurai from Chennai along with former Madras High Court judge V Parthiban, confirmed the timing after consultations with officials and temple priests.In a brief statement, he said, "deepam will be lit at 5 pm."The former judges later asked district officials to ensure the presence of the District Collector during the ceremony. Collector Nishant Krishna subsequently joined them, with the group expected to reach the Deepathoon atop the hill on foot by 4pm.Justice Vaidyanathan and Justice Parthiban performed pooja and rituals at the Thiruparankundram temple before handing over the cauldron to the priests for installation atop the stone pillar.The Deepathoon is being accessed with the help of scaffolding erected on the hill.Devotees and local residents gathered in large numbers at the foothills to witness the lighting ceremony.CRPF personnel have taken control of the hill, while authorities have restricted the number of people allowed to witness the ceremony from atop the hill to 50.Announcements were made over the public address system informing devotees of the restriction. Local officials said arrangements were complete, including the deployment of medical teams and ambulances to handle any emergency.The developments came a day after the Supreme Court issued a contempt notice to the Tamil Nadu government for what it termed a "willful and brazen" violation of its earlier directive on the Karthigai Deepam issue.The court had ordered that the ceremonial lamp be lit at the stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill on Saturday.
Article Summary: The traditional Karthigai Deepam will be lit atop the stone pillar (Deepathoon) on Thiruparankundram hill at 5pm on Saturday. Former Meghalaya High Court chief justice S Vaidyanathan said, following the Supreme Court's directive.

Article Title: A 1968 deal settled Mathura's temple-mosque dispute. Now, 58 years later, its validity is under fire
Article Text:
The 1968 agreement at the centre of the Mathura dispute, Krishnajanmabhoomi case (ANI file photo)

From 1968 agreement to 2026 HC order: How the Mathura dispute unfolded

What led to the 1968 compromise

What did the agreement provide

Why is the agreement being challenged

Sangh vs Trust: The legal distinction at the heart of the Mathura dispute

How the dispute returned to court

What Owaisi said about the 1968 Mathura agreement

What the HC has said so far

November 20 order: No final ruling on the 1968 settlement

NEW DELHI: A compromise signed on October 12, 1968, was meant to settle a dispute over land in Mathura where the Lord Krishna Janmabhoomi temple and the Shahi Eidgah mosque stand today. It laid down boundaries, specified which portions were to be handed over to each side and sought to prevent future disputes over access and construction.Almost 58 years later, that agreement has emerged as one of the most consequential documents in the Krishna Janmabhoomi-Shahi Eidgah dispute. Hindu litigants contend that the organisation which entered into the settlement had no authority to compromise over property belonging to the deity. The Muslim side, meanwhile, has relied on the agreement and the civil court decrees that followed it to argue that the dispute had already been settled.The Allahabad high court has not delivered a final verdict on the validity of the 1968 compromise. On November 20, 2026, it dismissed an application seeking to declare the agreement "null and void" and cancel the decrees passed in 1973 and 1974. However, the court made it clear that the relief sought could not be decided through an interim application, as it was also the main relief in some connected suits and would require a trial.The dismissal, the court said, was without affecting the merits of the other suits. With the next hearing scheduled for December 10, the agreement remains at the centre of a dispute involving ownership, the authority of the parties who signed it and the legal protection available to places of worship.The dispute concerns the Katra Keshav Dev complex in Mathura, with Hindu litigants claiming rights over a 13.37-acre property. The historical account of the site forms a significant part of the pleadings before the high court, though the claims about events centuries ago remain disputed.In its August 1, 2024 judgment, the Allahabad high court recorded the historical narrative advanced by the Hindu plaintiffs. According to their pleadings, a temple was built at the site in 1618 by Raja Veer Singh Bundela of Orchha. They alleged that Mughal ruler Aurangzeb partially demolished it in 1669-70 and raised a structure that came to be known as the Idgah mosque.The plaintiffs further stated that the British put 13.37 acres of land at Katra Keshav Dev up for public auction in 1815 and that Raja Patnimal of Benaras purchased it. His descendants later sold the property, with the transaction involving Seth Jugal Kishore Birla and the names of Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, Goswami Ganesh Dutt and Bhiken Lalji Aattrey appearing in the land's subsequent history.The 2024 judgment also refers to a trust deed dated March 9, 1951, through which the entire 13.37-acre property was dedicated to the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Trust. The document stated that one of the trust's objectives was to construct a temple at the birthplace of Lord Krishna.A key distinction in the present dispute is between this trust and the Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sangh, the organisation that later entered into the 1968 compromise. The Hindu plaintiffs argue that the two were separate legal entities and that the Seva Sangh neither owned the property nor had the authority to enter into an agreement affecting the deity's rights.The 1968 settlement arose from Civil Suit No. 43 of 1967, filed by the Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sangh against the Trust Shahi Masjid Idgah and others. The dispute also involved Muslim residents, including people described in the court record as Ghosis and other inhabitants who claimed to be tenants or licensees.The Allahabad high court's 2024 judgment records that the Idgah Trust had obtained permission from the Waqf Board through a letter dated September 9, 1968. A meeting held on October 8 that year adopted the agreement and authorised representatives to act on its behalf.The compromise was signed on October 12, 1968, presented before the court on October 17 and registered on November 22, according to the court record. The suit was eventually decreed on the basis of the compromise on July 20, 1973. A further decree followed on November 7, 1974.The agreement was not simply a broad understanding that both religious structures could continue to exist. It laid down specific arrangements for the land and physical boundaries between the two sides.Among other provisions, it required the northern and southern walls of the Idgah's "Kachchi Kursi" to be extended eastwards towards the railway line. The Idgah Trust was to get certain Muslim inhabitants living outside those walls vacated and hand over possession of the land to the Seva Sangh.It also dealt with land around the Idgah, including a portion on its western-northern side. The agreement provided for the removal of rubble from steps on the southern side, after which the Seva Sangh would take possession of the land.There were restrictions on construction facing the other side. The Trust was not to install doors, windows or grills in walls facing the Seva Sangh, or open drains or water outlets in that direction. The Seva Sangh was bound by similar restrictions. It was to divert water from the Idgah's outlets through pipes and construct a masonry drain at its own cost.The agreement further provided that both sides would file compromise applications in their pending cases after fulfilling the stipulated conditions. Either side could approach a court in the event of non-compliance.In effect, the document attempted to settle disputes over possession and the use of adjoining portions through a defined physical arrangement. It is this settlement, and whether the parties who signed it had the legal authority to do so, that is now being contested.The challenge rests substantially on the distinction between the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Trust and the Seva Sangh.The Hindu plaintiffs argue that the property had been vested in the Janmabhoomi Trust through the 1951 trust deed, while the Seva Sangh was a separate organisation. According to their pleadings, the Seva Sangh had no ownership rights and could not enter into a compromise affecting the interests of the deity.They also contend that neither the deity nor the Janmabhoomi Trust was a party to Civil Suit No. 43 of 1967 or the subsequent settlement. The plaintiffs argue that the Seva Sangh represented itself as having authority over the property and conceded land that it had no right to surrender.Advocate Kanu Agarwal told TOI, "The deity or the trust were never the parties to the Civil Suit No. 43 of 1967 or to the compromise deed dated 12.10.1968." He said the Seva Sangh was a distinct legal entity from the Janmabhoomi Trust and "prima facie was not the owner of the suit property".The 2024 high court judgment records these arguments, including the plaintiffs' claim that the compromise was fraudulent and that the decrees based on it should not bind the deity or devotees.The defendants have contested this position. The court record notes the argument that the compromise was entered into by recognised representatives, with the Idgah Trust having obtained the Waqf Board's permission. The Muslim side has also relied on the subsequent civil court decrees and argued that a challenge to the settlement cannot be brought through fresh proceedings.The central legal question, therefore, is whether the Seva Sangh had the authority to enter into the compromise, whether the settlement could bind the deity and the trust, and what legal effect should be given to the civil court decrees.The current round of litigation gained momentum in 2020, when a suit was filed by advocate Ranjana Agnihotri and six others on behalf of the deity and devotees. The plaintiffs sought ownership of the 13.37-acre property, removal of the Shahi Eidgah structure and restoration of the temple.The suit challenged the 1968 compromise and the decrees passed in 1973 and 1974, arguing that the settlement could not extinguish the rights of the deity because neither the deity nor the Janmabhoomi Trust was a party to the original proceedings.The issue soon became part of a wider legal and political debate around the Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act, 1991, which bars conversion of the religious character of a place of worship as it existed on August 15, 1947, subject to the Act's provisions and exceptions.On the Places of Worship Act, Advocate Kanu Agarwal said, "The compromise deed of 1968 has no bearing or connection with Places of Worship Act."He added while talking to TOI that the site's religious character and title "would require detailed trial wherein evidence is led by the parties".In May 2022, AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi questioned the revival of the dispute, referring to the 1968 settlement. "Sri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sangh and the Shahi Idgah Trust had resolved their issues by an agreement in 1968," he tweeted, adding, "Why revive it now?" Owaisi also invoked the Places of Worship Act.The Hindu side, however, maintained that the agreement was not binding on the deity and that its validity needed to be examined by a court.On August 1, 2024, the Allahabad high court rejected applications filed by the Muslim side seeking dismissal of the Hindu worshippers' suits at the threshold under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure.The court held that the suits could proceed and were not barred at that stage by the Places of Worship Act, the Waqf Act or the Limitation Act. This was a ruling on maintainability, not a final decision on ownership of the property or the validity of the 1968 agreement.The judgment examined arguments over the trust deed, the identity of the Seva Sangh, the original suit and the compromise. It observed that questions concerning the legality and validity of the agreement were factual issues that would require evidence during trial.The court's observations did not settle the dispute over title. Instead, they allowed the suits to move forward so that the competing claims could be examined through the judicial process.The litigation also moved to the question of a survey of the disputed premises. In December 2023, the high court had allowed an application seeking a court-monitored inspection. The Supreme Court stayed the implementation of that order in January 2024 in Special Leave Petition No. 481/2024.The survey issue remains linked to the Supreme Court proceedings. On November 21 that the high court had said it could not pass a fresh order on a similar survey application until the Supreme Court finally adjudicated the pending petition.The latest development has again brought the compromise into focus.In an order dated November 20, 2026, Justice Avnish Saxena dealt with four applications in Original Suit No. 7 of 2023. One of them, Application No. 56Ga2, sought a declaration that the October 12, 1968 agreement was null and void, cancellation of the 1973 and 1974 decrees and delivery of vacant possession of the disputed premises to the deity.The court noted that the suit was among 18 matters concerning the same property. Since the relief sought through the application was also the principal relief in some connected suits, it said the issue could not be adjudicated without a trial.The application was dismissed, but the order expressly stated that this was without affecting the merits of the other suits and that the application had not been taken up on its merits.In other words, the high court did not uphold the 1968 agreement or declare it invalid through this order. The question remains open for adjudication in the connected proceedings.The high court also dealt with applications concerning the representation of the deity and the impleadment of additional parties. It dismissed a plea seeking to implead descendants of Thakur Keshav Dev, observing that the deity was already represented through a next friend and that the purpose of adding the applicants had not been adequately explained.The next hearing in the dispute is scheduled for December 10.
Article Summary: The Allahabad high court has not delivered a final verdict on the validity of the 1968 compromise. The agreement remains at the centre of a dispute involving ownership, the authority of the parties who signed it and the legal protection available to places of worship. The dispute concerns the Katra Keshav Dev complex in Mathura, with Hindu litigants claiming rights over a 13.37-acre property.

Article Title: 'Self-interest over national interest': Mayawati takes swipe at parties over delimitation, backs women's quota
Article Text:
Mayawati calls for separate quota for SC/ST women within the 33% reservation, while questioning political interests behind delimitation

What the Centre's bills propose

NEW DELHI: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati on Saturday welcomed the Centre's move to implement 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies but called for a separate quota for women from Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST). She also took a swipe at parties over the proposed delimitation exercise, alleging that those in power at the Centre prioritise their own interests over national interest.In a series of posts on X, Mayawati said the BSP had consistently supported women's reservation and welcomed the government's recent decision. However, she said providing a separate share for SC/ST women within the 33% quota would have made the move historic.She said women from these communities had faced exploitation, oppression and neglect for centuries and needed greater opportunities to participate in electoral politics.Taking aim at the proposed delimitation exercise, the BSP chief said allegations of political and electoral considerations influencing the process were not new. The Centre has proposed three bills providing for a 50% increase in the existing number of seats in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies."In fact, whichever party is in power at the centre tends, in most such cases, to care less about the interests of the country and its people and to give greater importance to its own interests and self-interest. This is no secret to anyone," Mayawati said.She also referred to concerns over the proposed increase in seats and the delimitation process, alleging that constituency limits could be determined to serve political and electoral interests.Mayawati urged voters not to be swayed by religious, caste-based or regional considerations while choosing their representatives.The BSP chief reiterated her party's support for 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies. She said the party had long demanded its early implementation.However, she said a separate reservation for SC/ST women within the proposed quota would have helped address their historical exclusion from electoral politics."This would have given them an opportunity to participate properly in the country's electoral politics, which is plagued by narrow-mindedness, casteism, money and muscle power, and to move forward a little," she said.Mayawati added that the Centre should consider the demand, calling it appropriate and just.The Centre's proposed legislation provides for a 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to each state and Union Territory, as well as the total number of seats in state assemblies. If passed, the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha would rise to 850, while state assemblies could have up to 650 members.The proposal links the implementation of women's reservation, provided for under the 106th Constitutional Amendment in 2023, with a fresh delimitation exercise. The government aims to complete the process before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.The Opposition has supported women's reservation but objected to linking its implementation with delimitation. It has also demanded that the exercise use the latest Census data instead of the 2011 figures.The Centre has proposed using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies and determining seats reserved for SC/ST communities, while retaining the 1971 population basis for state-wise allocation of Lok Sabha seats until 2051.
Article Summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati calls for separate quota for SC/ST women within the 33% reservation. She also takes a swipe at parties over the proposed delimitation exercise, alleging that those in power prioritise their own interests over national interest. The Centre has proposed three bills providing for a 50% increase in the existing number of seats.

Article Title: 'SC must review its order': TN Congress as top court directs deepam lighting at Deepathoon
Article Text:
Manickam Tagore raises concerns over the deployment of central forces and the court's intervention in temple administration at Thiruparankundram

SC directs deepam lighting at Deepathoon

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu Congress committee (TNCC) president Manickam Tagore on Saturday urged the Supreme Court to review its order directing the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the Deepathoon stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai. He raised concerns over federal principles, religious harmony and the respective roles of the judiciary, state government and temple administration."Concern over federal principles and religious harmony - the Supreme Court must review its order! The Tamil Nadu Congress Committee expresses its deep concern over the Supreme Court’s order in the matter of lighting the lamp at Thiruparankundram in Madurai. Respecting and upholding religious beliefs and worship rights, as well as safeguarding harmony among various communities and the peaceful social environment prevailing in Tamil Nadu, is everyone’s foremost responsibility," he said in a post on X.Tagore questioned the court's actions concerning temple administration, its appointment of a committee comprising retired judges and the involvement of central paramilitary forces in security arrangements."In this context, the court’s actions concerning temple administration, its appointment of a committee comprising retired judges, and the involvement of central paramilitary forces in security arrangements raise important questions about the jurisdictions of the judiciary, the state administration, and temple administration.In such sensitive matters, not only must the rule of law be upheld, but the administrative responsibilities of the democratically elected state government and the federal framework established by the Indian Constitution must also be duly taken into account," he said.He also stressed that the responsibilities of the elected state government and the federal structure under the Constitution must be considered in sensitive matters."Furthermore, the court’s order must be framed in a way that fosters trust and peace among all parties without hurting the religious sentiments of any party. The Tamil Nadu Congress Committee’s firm position is that the rule of law must be upheld in the country, while Tamil Nadu’s peace, religious harmony, and constitutional values must be protected without any harm. Therefore, on behalf of the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee, we urge the Supreme Court to review its order in this matter," he said.The Congress leader's remarks came amid a dispute over the lighting of the ceremonial Karthigai deepam at the Deepathoon stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram Hill, near the Sikandar Badhusha Dargah.On Friday, the Supreme Court directed that the lamp be lit at the stone pillar on November 28. It also allowed devotees to participate in the ceremony and ordered the deployment of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to ensure its smooth conduct.Following the directive, one company of CRPF personnel was deployed in the area for security and surveillance duties.The Supreme Court bench also found wilful disobedience of its earlier order, observing that the lamp had not been lit at the Deepathoon on November 24 despite its directions and an undertaking given by the Madurai district collector before the Madras High Court.The controversy intensified after the Maha Deepam was lit near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple during the annual Karthigai Deepam festival on November 24 instead of at the Deepathoon.
Article Summary: Manickam Tagore raises concerns over deployment of central forces and the court's intervention in temple administration at Thiruparankundram Hill. He raised concerns over federal principles, religious harmony and the respective roles of the judiciary, state government and temple administration. His remarks came amid a dispute over the lighting of the ceremonial Karthigai deepam.

Article Title: Gavai cites two examples to buttress caste bias claim
Article Text:
Justice Gavai said he was highlighting the issue as he was part of the collegium when the judge was transferred from one HC to a smaller HC (J'khand) and was heading collegium when he was transferred to smallest HC (Tripura).

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Slamming the Supreme Court collegium’s recent recommendation for transfer of Tripura HC Chief Justice MS Ramachandra Rao as the chief justice of Karnataka HC, former CJI B R Gavai Friday asked whether the judge, who was transferred multiple times on punitive considerations, was being rewarded with a bigger and more prominent high court just because he belonged to an upper caste.Without naming Justice Rao, the ex-CJI in his letter to President Droupadi Murmu said the recommendation “raises several unanswered questions as to how a judge transferred multiple times on punitive considerations is now being recommended to be chief justice of a much bigger and prominent high court”.On Nov 26, TOI had reported that Justice Rao, son of former Supreme Court judge Justice M Jagannadha Rao, was appointed as judge of Andhra Pradesh HC in 2012 and had opted for Telangana HC in 2019 after the state’s bifurcation.He was transferred to the Punjab and Haryana HC and then made the chief justice of the Himachal Pradesh HC. Later, he was shifted to the Jharkhand and Tripura high courts.“A chief justice who was transferred from one high court to another smaller HC and thereafter from that HC to one of the smallest HCs of the country has now been rewarded for being from a particular community, by transfer to a prominent high court,” the ex-CJI said.Sources in the top court said serving Supreme Court judges from Karnataka, one of whom is in the collegium and is slated to become the first woman CJI next year, were prominent backers of the proposal to transfer Justice Rao as CJ of Karnataka.The Centre is yet to act on the recommendations, which include transfer of Karnataka HC CJ Vibhu Bakhru to Jharkhand HC and appointment of Justice Vivek Singh Thakur of Himachal HC as the chief justice of Tripura HC.Again, without naming Justice Bakhru, former CJI Gavai said the transfer of the “meritorious and hardworking CJ of Karnataka” to a smaller high court to make way for Justice Rao not only demoralises meritorious judges like Justice Bakhru but “also has a chilling effect on all hard-working judges, including persons belonging to marginalised sections of society”.Justice Gavai said he was highlighting the issue (relating to Justice Rao) as he was part of the collegium when the judge was transferred from one HC to a smaller HC (Jharkhand) and was heading the collegium when he was transferred to the smallest high court (Tripura).
Article Summary: Supreme Court collegium’s recent recommendation for transfer of Tripura HC Chief Justice MS Ramachandra Rao as the chief justice of Karnataka HC. Former CJI B R Gavai asked whether the judge was being rewarded with a bigger and more prominent high court just because he belonged to an upper caste.

Article Title: Mirwaiz under house arrest after Sheshnag, Vande Mataram criticism; barred from leading Friday prayers
Article Text:
Mirwaiz Umar Farooq

SRINAGAR: The J&K administration on Friday placed Hurriyat Conference chairman and Kashmir’s chief cleric, Mirwaiz Umar Farooq , under house arrest and barred him from leading Friday prayers at the historic Jamia Masjid in Srinagar.Mirwaiz attributed his latest house arrest to his criticism of alleged construction work near the ecologically fragile Sheshnag Lake and the opposition expressed by the Mutahida Majlis-e-Ulama (MMU), an organisation led by him, to the rendition of Vande Mataram at the waqf board function on Monday.“In keeping with the tradition of putting me under house arrest on Fridays, ahead of visiting Jamia Masjid for sermon and prayers, I have again been put under house arrest today. I had anticipated this, as I had raised people’s grave concerns over the disaster waiting to happen in the eco-fragile region of Sheshnag after the viral visuals, and later the recitation of Vande Mataram at the religious function of the waqf board, I would be punished this Friday by being put under house arrest,” Mirwaiz said.“It would do the ruling regime much better if instead of applying pressure on me, it understood the sensitivity and impact these issues have on the people of Jammu & Kashmir, whose welfare it claims to hold dear, and desists from imposing things that cause people hurt and concern,” he said.On Wednesday, several Muslim clerics who attended a J&K Waqf Board function where Vande Mataram was played in full expressed regret and said they had prayed for repentance, as the national song triggered a religious controversy in Kashmir.Monday’s waqf board function was attended by Union minority affairs minister Kiren Rijiju, waqf board chairperson and BJP member Dr Darakhshan Andrabi, Lok Sabha MP Mian Altaf Ahmad and others.All six stanzas of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay’s 1875 poem Vande Mataram were played at the event in accordance with a Union home ministry protocol directive issued earlier this year that mandated the full version at state functions, official events and legislative sessions.On Thursday, MMU, an amalgam of religious organisations and institutions, said there was no legal obligation to play the song at an official function, and criticised the waqf board for playing it at an event organised by an institution entrusted with safeguarding Muslim religious endowments. “Any expression or practice that attributes divinity to the motherland is contrary to the fundamental Islamic belief of Tawheed and is, therefore, un-Islamic and impermissible for Muslims,” MMU had said.PDP president Mehbooba Mufti said she strongly condemns the continued house arrest of Mirwaiz, particularly on Fridays when he is prevented from offering prayers and delivering his sermon at Jamia Masjid.Police have not issued any statement on the issue.
Article Summary: Mirwaiz blames his latest house arrest on his criticism of alleged construction work near the ecologically fragile Sheshnag Lake. The Hurriyat Conference chairman and Kashmir’s chief cleric, Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, is barred from leading Friday prayers at Jamia Masjid.

NEW DELHI: DMK chief MK Stalin on Friday accused the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government of bringing "disgrace" to the state by failing to present a strong defence before the Supreme Court in the Deepam case.His remarks came hours after the Supreme Court came down heavily on the Tamil Nadu government for defying its order in the case, observing that it was prima facie in contempt of court."The incompetent TVK government has brought unprecedented peril to Tamil Nadu’s history—threatening our traditions, religious harmony, and state rights! Article Title: 70-year-old Karnataka woman gifts property to daughter-in-law, approaches tribunal to reclaim it after 22 years; Karnataka HC says Senior Citizens Act cannot undo old transfer but retains Rs 4,000 mon
Article Text:
AI Generated Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





BENGALURU: A gift made in 2000 cannot be undone using a law that came into force eight years later, the Karnataka High Court has ruled, overturning a tribunal's decision to cancel a 70-year-old woman's transfer of property to her daughter-in-law. The court, however, retained the latter's obligation to pay the elderly woman Rs 4,000 every month for the rest of her life.The dispute arose from a registered gift deed dated July 29, 2000, through which the woman transferred her properties to her daughter-in-law and handed over possession. The deed stated that the transfer was made out of love and affection and to protect the properties, as the woman's son was habituated to certain vices.The arrangement remained in place for nearly 22 years before the elderly woman approached the Senior Citizens Maintenance Tribunal, seeking to get the transfer reversed. She accused her daughter-in-law of securing the deed through fraud and misrepresentation.The tribunal first rejected her plea on January 5, 2023, saying that a dispute over cancellation of a gift deed had to be dealt with by a civil court. But it subsequently passed another order on July 3, 2023, cancelling the deed and directing revenue officials to alter the property records.This was done without issuing notice to the daughter-in-law.Challenging the decision, the daughter-in-law told the high court that the transfer had taken place in 2000, whereas the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act came into force only on April 1, 2008. She argued that the provisions of the Act could not be used to set aside a transaction completed before the legislation existed.The high court found merit in the argument. It pointed out that the gift deed was registered and that the elderly woman had waited almost 22 years before approaching the tribunal. The court said the 2007 Act was prospective in nature and could not be used to invalidate property transfers made before April 1, 2008. It held that the tribunal had no jurisdiction to cancel the registered deed and quashed its decision to interfere with the property transfer.The daughter-in-law had, however, expressed her willingness to continue paying Rs 4,000 a month to her mother-in-law despite challenging the tribunal's order. The court allowed the maintenance direction to remain in force, meaning the daughter-in-law will have to pay the elderly woman Rs 4,000 every month throughout her lifetime.
Article Summary: Karnataka High Court overturns a tribunal's decision to cancel a 70-year-old woman's transfer of property to her daughter-in-law. The court, however, retained the latter's obligation to pay the elderly woman Rs 4,000 every month for the rest of her life. The dispute arose from a registered gift deed dated July 29, 2000.

Article Title: Serena Williams' $1.4 million childhood home was caught in $600,000 debt battle as father's estranged wife faced bankruptcy setback
Article Text:
Serena Williams (Getty Images)

Serena Williams ' childhood home became the centre of a $600,000 debt dispute

Serena and Venus Williams' family home was eventually sold

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Before Serena and Venus Williams became two of tennis's biggest names, their family home in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, held memories of a very different life. Nearly three decades after Richard Williams bought the property, the four-bedroom house became the centre of a bitter financial and legal dispute. In April 2024, a judge dismissed another bankruptcy filing by Richard's wife, Lakeisha Williams, leaving the property exposed to foreclosure. The case involved an estimated $600,000 debt, a disputed loan and allegations surrounding the transfer of the family home.Richard Williams reportedly purchased the property in 1995 for approximately $355,000. The house later became closely linked to the early years of Serena and Venus, who trained under their father's guidance before reaching the top of professional tennis.However, the family's history with the property took a difficult turn after Lakeisha faced mounting financial problems. Court proceedings involved allegations that she had forged Richard's signature to transfer the house into her name and secure a loan of approximately $279,000 from lender David Simon.The money was reportedly intended to support a trucking business, which eventually failed. Lakeisha disputed aspects of the allegations and said she had struggled to provide for herself and her son.The debt reportedly grew to around $600,000 after interest and other costs.The property was valued at approximately $1.4 million. Lakeisha had attempted to protect it through bankruptcy proceedings, but the court dismissed her latest Chapter 13 filing in April 2024. She had also struggled to maintain a proposed repayment plan requiring monthly payments of around $10,000.The bankruptcy ruling initially raised the prospect that the property would be sold to repay creditors. However, the story took another turn before the planned auction.In August 2024, the house was reportedly sold for approximately $1.2 million to Hardy Firm LLC. Reports said the sale helped settle around $436,000 in outstanding debt, preventing the property from going through the planned foreclosure auction.The identity and connections of the buyer also attracted attention. The Sun reported links between the company and people associated with Lakeisha, although those connections did not establish who ultimately controlled the property.The family dispute also appeared to ease. Later reports said Richard and Lakeisha had reconciled and resumed living together, despite years of legal conflict.For Serena and Venus, the property remained part of the story of their early lives. But the financial battle showed how a home associated with a sporting legacy could become entangled in years of debt, allegations and family disagreements.
Article Summary: Richard Williams reportedly purchased the property in 1995 for approximately $355,000. The house later became closely linked to the early years of Serena and Venus, who trained under their father's guidance. Court proceedings involved allegations that she had forged Richard's signature to transfer the house into her name.

Article Title: 'Goat', 'cow' or 'bibi': Taliban's latest crackdown strips Afghan women of their names
Article Text:
Afghan women allegedly subjected to degrading labels under Taliban rule

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Taliban authorities in Afghanistan’s northern Balkh province have reportedly banned the use of women’s names on official documents, including medical records and prescriptions. Healthcare workers have also been instructed to address female patients as “Bibi”, meaning grandmother or old woman.The reported order, highlighted by Spanish newspaper El País and based on accounts cited from Afghan outlet Zan Times and The Guardian, has raised concerns that the restriction could be extended to other parts of the country.According to the reports, hospital staff and other public employees in Balkh have been told not to use women’s names. Afghan women’s rights activist Lalah Osmany, based in Germany, told El País that testimonies from women, doctors and civil rights activists indicated that some women were also being addressed in degrading terms such as “goat” or “cow”.“This is a systematic process of dehumanization,” Osmany told the newspaper.An Afghan activist speaking under a pseudonym also confirmed the reported order to El País, although she said it had so far been ignored.Zubaida Akbar, who heads the Afghanistan programme at women’s rights organisation Femena, warned that the restriction could eventually become nationwide. She pointed to previous instances in which measures introduced locally were subsequently expanded across Afghanistan. Femena has documented more than 144 decrees restricting women’s rights, according to El País.The reported move comes amid wider restrictions imposed on women since the Taliban returned to power in 2021. Girls have been barred from education beyond the age of 12, while women have been excluded from most professions and face restrictions on speaking in public.The restrictions have also affected access to healthcare. In several provinces, male doctors have reportedly been barred from treating female patients. Women are among the few groups permitted to work in healthcare, but the Taliban banned women from training in medical fields in December 2024.UNICEF has warned that the restrictions have created a “dual crisis”, as trained women healthcare workers leave or retire without younger women being allowed to replace them.A 2024 UN report also highlighted difficulties Afghan women face in obtaining civil documents. Women generally need a male chaperone to complete the process, creating barriers for those in women-led households or those whose male relatives cannot accompany them.Such documents are often necessary to access healthcare, education, humanitarian assistance and banking services.Despite the restrictions, some women continue to operate underground businesses and secret schools. In an Associated Press report published on November 17, a Kabul beauty salon owner, whose identity was withheld for her safety, said: “But now, they won’t even allow that; for women in Afghanistan, working has become a crime.”An assistant teacher at a secret school told the AP: “We are absolutely terrified of that possibility,” referring to the prospect of arrest.
Article Summary: Taliban authorities reportedly ban use of women's names on official documents. Healthcare workers have also been instructed to address female patients as ‘Bibi’, meaning grandmother or old woman. Move comes amid wider restrictions imposed on women since the Taliban returned to power in 2021.
