Article Title: Widowed mother lets son and daughter-in-law stay in one room 'out of love and affection', they refuse to leave and claim a stake; Delhi court upholds eviction, gives them 30 days to vacate
Article Text:
A widowed mother sits inside a room discussing property documents with her son and daughter-in-law (AI image)

(With inputs from PTI)





NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has upheld an eviction order directing a man and his wife to vacate a room in the house of his widowed mother, who had allowed them to stay there temporarily out of love and affection.District judge Sumit Dalal dismissed the couple's appeal against a trial court order asking them to hand over possession of the room to the 65-year-old woman. The court has given them 30 days to vacate the premises.In an order dated November 5, the court said, "The defendants have admitted that they were permitted to reside in one room 'temporarily' out of love and affection. They are, on their own showing, licensees, whose licence was revocable at the will of the plaintiff."It observed that a son and daughter-in-law do not gain any legal right to continue living in their parents' house simply because they were allowed to stay there for a period of time.The court also clarified that the eviction decree applied only to one room in the house, and not the entire property.The woman had purchased the property in 2017 for Rs 11.75 lakh and allowed her son and daughter-in-law to occupy a room on the ground floor.According to her, the arrangement was temporary, with the couple required to pay monthly rent of Rs 4,000 and look after her.She alleged that they stopped paying rent after a few months, refused to vacate the room and repeatedly assured her that they would leave once they found alternative accommodation.Challenging the eviction order, the couple claimed they had contributed towards purchasing and constructing the house and had spent money on its renovation. They also alleged that their previous counsel had made admissions in the written statement without their knowledge.The court rejected these arguments, noting that both defendants had signed the written statement, acknowledged the mother's ownership of the property and admitted that they had been allowed to stay temporarily.It said the couple could not subsequently retract these admissions and put forward an entirely different case claiming ownership rights.The court also dismissed their plea of adverse possession, observing that possession which began with the owner's permission could not be considered adverse.It held that the couple's claims concerning their contribution to the construction, agricultural land and jurisdiction did not raise any triable issue that could prevent the possession decree.However, the court clarified that the suit would continue before the trial court in relation to the remaining reliefs, which would be decided independently on their merits.
Article Summary: A Delhi court has upheld an eviction order directing a man and his wife to vacate a room in the house of his widowed mother. District judge Sumit Dalal dismissed the couple's appeal against a trial court order asking them to hand over possession of the room to the 65-year-old woman. The woman had purchased the property in 2017 for Rs 11.75 lakh.

Article Title: 17-year-old alleges sexual assault inside Kolkata BJP office, case filed against 4 workers
Article Text:
The Uriapara area of Beleghata, where the ruckus took place





KOLKATA: A 17-year-old boy was allegedly confined, beaten and sexually assaulted inside a BJP office in Beleghata’s Uriyapara area, prompting police to register a case under the Pocso Act against four party workers, including three women.The case was lodged hours after a woman leading a rival BJP faction alleged that another group had threatened her and forcibly evicted her from the office.The alleged assault took place on Sunday amid tensions between two BJP factions vying for control of the “temporary” party office.The teenager told police that around 8.15 pm, he was walking past the office when he was called inside. A male worker allegedly locked the door, following which three women sexually assaulted him. When he resisted, the man allegedly restrained him while the women continued assaulting him.Hearing his screams, two women known to him rescued him. He was taken to NRS Hospital. On Monday, he approached Beleghata police with his medical report and lodged a complaint.BJP’s North Kolkata district president Tamoghna Ghosh said, “I am not aware of the matter. I will look into it.” Local MLA and Trinamool spokesperson Kunal Ghosh said, “The BJP’s factional fighting in this area has created complete disorder.Cops should conduct an impartial investigation.”Senior Lalbazar officers said the sections invoked carry a maximum sentence of less than seven years and investigators would issue notices instead of immediately arresting the accused.“However, we are ascertaining the age of the minor and ascertaining the chain of events before sending the notices in the next one week,” an officer said. Preliminary probe suggest the incident stemmed from an old personal enmity involving a dispute over possession of the premises, police sources said.The premises previously housed a local club’s free medical camp and allegedly a Trinamool office before being occupied by a woman BJP worker. Another BJP faction opposed her occupation of the premises. “Both cases are being probed simultaneously,” an officer said.
Article Summary: A 17-year-old boy was allegedly confined, beaten and sexually assaulted inside a BJP office in Beleghata’s Uriyapara area. The alleged assault took place on Sunday amid tensions between two BJP factions vying for control of the “temporary” party office. Police have filed a case under the Pocso Act against four party workers, including three women.

Article Title: Released after 7 years in jail, man arrested for 'sexual assault' on 10-year-old in northwest Delhi park
Article Text:
Ismail Khan Wala Bagh in northwest Delhi

About the accused





NEW DELHI: A 10-year-old girl was Tuesday allegedly sexually assaulted by a 35-year-old man inside Ismail Khan Wala Bagh in northwest Delhi. The suspect was caught and thrashed by locals, who then handed him over to police. A case under BNS sections pertaining to sexual assault and relevant sections of Pocso Act has been registered.The man, identified as Rajesh , a resident of northwest Delhi, works as a carpenter. He was previously convicted in a 2018 case involving the sexual assault of a minor in Swaroop Nagar and sentenced to seven years in prison. He was released from jail a few months ago, police sources said.The incident comes two months after three men posing as policemen allegedly threatened and gang-raped a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park in southeast Delhi’s Kalkaji.A PCR call regarding Tuesday’s incident was received around 11.30am, following which a team from the local police station rushed to the spot. Initial inquiry revealed the girl, a Class IV student, was playing hide-and-seek at the park when she spotted Rajesh urinating. On seeing her, he allegedly attempted to lure her towards him.“He did not drag her; she went with him on her own. He allegedly attempted to disrobe her and unbuttoned two buttons of her clothing,” a police official said.Hearing the child’s screams, people in the vicinity rushed to her aid, caught the suspect and thrashed him before handing him over to police. Police denied claims that the girl was passing through the park on her way to a relative’s house after school.Police sources said the suspect was unmarried and estranged from his family. Investigators are probing whether he was under the influence of any intoxicating substance at the time of the incident, and have sent his blood samples for testing.His electronic devices have been seized to examine his internet search history. Cops will also check if he was involved in other such incidents that may have gone unreported since his release from prison.The incident, meanwhile, has again raised questions over security arrangements at city parks. Police sources said only one guard was deployed at the sprawling park at the time of the incident, despite at least four-five personnel required for effective monitoring.“We had flagged the security concern with the authorities concerned, and will pursue the matter further,” a police source said.DDA said the security personnel at the park acted promptly, immediately alerted police, facilitating the suspect’s arrest.“DDA has already put in place requisite safety and security arrangements at the park, including 47 functional light points, a boundary wall, entry/exit gates, women and child safety awareness boards, and round-the-clock deployment of six security guards, with two guards in each shift… DDA remains committed to ensuring a safe environment in its parks,” it stated.
Article Summary: A 10-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted by a man inside Ismail Khan Wala Bagh in northwest Delhi. The suspect was caught and thrashed by locals, who then handed him over to police. A case under BNS sections pertaining to sexual assault and relevant sections of Pocso Act has been registered.

Article Title: Raja Bhaiya to contest from Kunda again as party announces first list for 2027 UP polls
Article Text:
Raja Bhaiya, the party president, will contest again from his stronghold of Kunda.





PRAYAGRAJ: Jansatta Dal Loktantrik on Thursday announced its first list of three candidates, including party president Raghuraj Pratap Singh aka Raja Bhaiya, for the 2027 state assembly polls.While Raja Bhaiya will contest again from his stronghold of Kunda, sitting party MLA Vinod Saroj will try his luck from Babaganj assembly seat in Pratapgarh district.This time, the party has also decided to contest from Vishwanathganj assembly seat in Pratapgarh district and announced Kuldeep Patel, representative of the zila panchayat chairman, as its candidate.Raja Bhaiya launched 'Jansatta Dal (Loktantrik)' on Nov 30, 2018, at a massive rally in Lucknow, marking the completion of his 25 years in politics as an independent legislator. It was then said that he formed a separate party following requests from his supporters after an online survey. Prior to this, he had contested elections as an independent candidate for nearly 25 years.Raja Bhaiya, the MLA from Kunda, has been elected seven consecutive times since he first won in 1993 as an independent candidate. Subsequently, he went on to win in 1996, 2002, 2007, 2012 and 2017. In the 2022 assembly elections, he secured victory on the ticket of his own party, Jansatta Dal (Loktantrik).In the 2022 Kunda assembly elections, Raja Bhaiya secured 99,612 votes and defeated his nearest rival, Gulshan Yadav of the Samajwadi Party, by a margin of over 30,000 votes.
Article Summary: Raja Bhaiya, the party president, will contest again from his stronghold of Kunda. Sitting party MLA Vinod Saroj will try his luck from Babaganj assembly seat in Pratapgarh district. Kuldeep Patel, representative of the zila panchayat chairman, as its candidate.

Article Title: Kolkata man 'conceals' HIV+ status from partner, arrested after pre-marital tests
Article Text:
A woman files a formal cheating complaint before a Kolkata police officer after her partner concealed his HIV status. (AI image)

'Knowingly' endangered partners





KOLKATA: What began as a digital romance two years ago ended at a south Kolkata police station on Wednesday after a nurse’s insistence on pre-marital health screenings exposed a devastating secret: her partner had allegedly concealed his HIV-positive status throughout their relationship. Based on the woman’s complaint, Bansdroni cops have arrested the accused, an employee at a private firm.According to cops, the couple connected on social media roughly two years ago. Over time, regular conversations blossomed into a relationship. They travelled together frequently and eventually became physically intimate, with the complainant believing they were building a shared future.However, cracks began appearing in their relationship recently when the woman broached the subject of marriage and starting a family. According to police sources, the man repeatedly evaded the topic, offering excuses whenever wedding plans came up.His reluctance aroused her suspicions. Drawing on her medical background, she decided that both should undergo routine diagnostic check-ups as part of their pre-wedding preparations.Initially, the man flatly refused to take the tests. Eventually, faced with his girlfriend’s persistent requests, he agreed.The diagnostic reports revealed the man was HIV-positive.Devastated by the discovery, the woman immediately underwent a medical test herself. In her formal complaint, she alleged the accused had been aware of his medical condition long before entering into a physical relationship with her, deliberately keeping her in the dark.She further alleged he had disclosed having had physical relationships with several other women in the past.Feeling betrayed and endangered, the nurse lodged a formal complaint accusing him of cheating and breach of trust. “Based on her allegations, we arrested the man on Wednesday. A case has been registered against him under multiple charges, including fraud,” an officer said.
Article Summary: Kolkata woman files cheating complaint after partner conceals his HIV status. Couple connected on social media two years ago. She insisted on pre-wedding health screenings as part of their preparations. The diagnostic reports revealed the man was HIV-positive.

Article Title: Engine fails, instructor and trainee pilot crash-land aircraft in Hyderabad's Golconda Cantt
Article Text:
The accident occurred around 1pm, nearly two hours after the aircraft had taken off from Begumpet airport for the training exercise.

Previous crashes





HYDERABAD: A trainer aircraft of the Telangana State Aviation Academy (TSAA) suffered an engine failure mid-air and crash-landed at the Golconda Cantonment parade grounds on Thursday afternoon. The trainee pilot and her instructor escaped with minor injuries.The two-seater Cessna, which had taken off from Begumpet airport on a training sortie, was flying at around 3,000 feet when its engine failed. The trainee and instructor managed to steer the aircraft towards an open stretch inside Golconda Cantonment and attempted a forced landing. The aircraft, however, struck a tree while coming down and was damaged.“After observing the engine had failed, the pilots decided to force-land it. On seeing the plain location at parade grounds inside the Golconda Cantonment, they decided to land the aircraft there. They almost successfully did, but the aircraft came in touch with a tree leading to the accident,’’ an official from the academy said.The accident occurred around 1pm, nearly two hours after the aircraft had taken off from Begumpet airport for the training exercise.Military personnel rushed to the damaged aircraft and helped bring the two occupants out. They were later shifted to a private hospital.A senior Hyderabad police officer told TOI that both were safe and being treated for minor injuries.An academy official said this was the first accident in the last 20 years involving a TSAA trainer aircraft.The unusual sight of a light aircraft coming down inside the Cantonment drew the attention of civilians in the vicinity, with many rushing towards the area to find out what had happened.Asked if the incident had triggered panic inside the Cantonment, an official said: “It was not a military aircraft. They also understood that it was a training aircraft.’’DCP (Golconda zone) J Raghavendra Reddy told TOI that a case will be registered and a letter will be sent to officials of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) to conduct a probe on the cause of the accident.“Officials of the DGCA came to the spot and took stock,” he said.
Article Summary: The two-seater Cessna was flying at around 3,000 feet when its engine failed. The trainee and instructor managed to steer the aircraft towards an open stretch inside Golconda Cantonment. The aircraft, however, struck a tree while coming down and was damaged.

Article Title: Fed up with wives' constant quarrels, 2 Jharkhand brothers kill them, bury bodies; lodge missing complaint
Article Text:
Four family members from Gumla district were arrested for the alleged murder of two women, Mini Priya and Radhika Kumari.





GUMLA: Four members of a family, including two brothers, were arrested in Jharkhand's Gumla district for allegedly killing two women, transporting their bodies in an ambulance and burying them in neighbouring Simdega district, police said on Wednesday.The deceased, identified as Mini Priya (28) and Radhika Kumari (20), were married to brothers Shivshankar Sahu and Navin Sahu, respectively. Police said the brothers were allegedly angered by a long-standing dispute between the two women, who had recently reconciled.The arrested accused were identified as Shivshankar, Navin, their father Sameshwar Sahu and mother Tileshwari Devi. The family hails from Samsera village under Gumla Sadar police station limits, where the murders allegedly took place.According to police, the women were allegedly killed with an axe following domestic disputes on Monday. The brothers, one of whom works as an ambulance driver, then transported the bodies in an ambulance and buried them in a deserted area in Simdega district.Their bodies were later recovered from a ditch near a dhaba in Arani Nekdarn village in Simdega and sent to Sadar Hospital in Gumla for postmortem examination.Police also recovered an axe allegedly used in the killings based on the accused's confession.The case came to light after police received a complaint from Hema Devi of Nagfeni Raputoli village under Sisai police station limits. The accused had initially approached police claiming that the two women had gone missing without informing them. However, their statements raised suspicion during questioning.Gumla SP Harish Bin Zaman said the accused confessed to the crime during sustained interrogation. He added that further investigation was underway to establish the circumstances behind the murders, including the role of other family members.The accused have been booked under sections 103(1), 238 and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Article Summary: Four family members from Gumla district were arrested for the alleged murder of two women, Mini Priya and Radhika Kumari. According to police, the women were allegedly killed with an axe following domestic disputes on Monday. The brothers allegedly transported the bodies in an ambulance and buried them in a deserted area in Simdega district.

Article Title: Delhi ‘drug syndicate’ run by mother, son, daughter and relative; all 4 face preventive detention
Article Text:
Delhi Police personnel serve detention orders and escort suspects in a narrow residential lane in West Sagarpur during crackdown (AI image)





NEW DELHI: Behind the closed doors of a house in southwest Delhi's West Sagarpur, an entire family was allegedly running a drug syndicate, with a woman, her son, daughter and another female relative suspected of being part of the network.Now, all four are facing preventive detention under the stringent Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (PITNDPS) Act while police try to dismantle the alleged family-run operation.Delhi govt's home department has forwarded detention orders against 11 people under the PITNDPS Act, 1988, according to an official communication dated Nov 23. The letter, addressed to the superintendent of Tihar Jail, directs prison authorities to take necessary action on the orders, which were accompanied by individual grounds of detention.The West Sagarpur family accounts for four of the 11 people named in the communication.According to police records, the alleged network involved two sisters, one of whom had 30 previous cases registered against her since 1996, while the other had 25 cases dating back to 1995.The latter's two children, a daughter and a son, were also allegedly involved in criminal activities, with eight cases registered against the daughter since 2016 and five against the son since 2018.The four are collectively involved in 68 cases. Police sources said the alleged drug supply source was in Firozpur, Punjab."The family was allegedly operating a syndicate, which needed to be broken. The anti-narcotics cell of South West district examined various aspects of the network, including its financial dealings, and built a strong case for invoking the PITNDPS Act," a source said.Investigators are also looking into properties allegedly acquired by the family using proceeds from drug sales. Sources said the financial trail is being examined to identify assets that may have been purchased through the alleged illegal trade.The objective, they added, is to strike at the financial foundations of the suspected network rather than merely target those allegedly involved in selling narcotics.The remaining names are spread across the capital. Two individuals each belong to Outer North and East districts, while one each is from Outer and North districts. Another person from Dwarka has also been named.The PITNDPS Act allows preventive detention to curb illicit trafficking in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. The stringent provision is used against people suspected of continuing such activities and is aimed at preventing them from carrying on illicit drug trafficking.Police sources said the latest action was prompted by concerns that the accused continued to engage in criminal activities, posing a challenge to law and order. The wider crackdown is aimed at disrupting suspected drug networks operating across Delhi.Earlier in Aug, a 51-year-old drug trafficker was arrested and booked under the PITNDPS Act. Dharamveer Singh, a resident of Inderpuri, became a major supplier of illegal ganja.The drug was smuggled from south India to the capital. He also masterminded an attack on a narcotics branch team in 2022.
Article Summary: Delhi govt's home department has forwarded detention orders against 11 people. Alleged network involved two sisters, one of whom had 30 previous cases registered against her since 1996, while the other had 25 cases dating back to 1995. Police sources said the alleged drug supply source was in Firozpur, Punjab.

Article Title: 'Police have no regard for life, liberty': MP high court slams DGP Kailash Makwana, Gwalior SSP over 31 of 34 unanswered requisitions in prisoner's bail case; reserve inspector, constable suspended
Article Text:
The court questioned whether senior police officers had verified the records before submitting comments and accused the police hierarchy of attempting to shield those responsible for the lapses.





BHOPAL: The Madhya Pradesh high court has come down heavily on senior police officers, including the state DGP and Gwalior SSP, over alleged suppression of facts and failure to act on official communications concerning a prisoner's bail plea.The court questioned whether senior police officers had verified the records before submitting comments and accused the police hierarchy of attempting to shield those responsible for the lapses.A division bench of justice GS Ahluwalia and justice Anuradha Shukla, in an order passed on November 26, expressed serious concern over the police department's conduct, observing that its senior officers appeared to have little regard for the life and liberty of prisoners or the law.The case relates to a criminal appeal filed by Ramjeet alias Ramjilal and others. During the proceedings, the court examined 34 requisitions received by a reserve inspector in connection with the matter. Only three were answered, while the remaining 31 were allegedly left unattended.The court noted that the communications were available in the reserve inspector's records. It questioned how DGP Kailash Makwana could submit comments claiming there was no basis to infer apathy on the part of the police department when 31 requisitions remained unanswered.The bench also observed that the DGP's comments were neither signed by him nor accompanied by an affidavit. When it considered issuing notice to the DGP, Gwalior SSP Dharmveer Singh told the court that senior officers, including the in-charge DIG, had verified the records but had not informed the DGP about the unanswered requisitions.The SSP further submitted that the comments filed before the high court had been approved by the DGP.Questioning this explanation, the bench observed that either the DGP was aware of the correct facts or had endorsed the police department's conduct without verifying the records.The court also questioned the basis for the DGP's comments in light of the SSP's decision to order a preliminary inquiry and seek a month's time to examine the matter.Appearing before the court, the SSP said he had suspended Reserve Inspector Ranjeet Singh Sikarwar and a constable. He later sought time to explain his decision to order a preliminary inquiry, saying he had been undergoing training and was unaware of the case details.The bench rejected this explanation, observing that the relevant facts had already been set out in its earlier orders and that the SSP was aware of the developments.In another serious development, the court flagged irregularities in the handling of official documents by the office of the additional advocate general.It noted that comments sought from the DGP had been shown to the court on November 16, with an assurance that they would be filed the same day. However, they were submitted only on November 23.The court also found that a compliance report shown on November 25 and cleared for filing by the regular Reader, Hariom Sharma, had not been uploaded to the court's electronic portal.On examining the physical file, the bench found that Mohd Sabir, a substitute Reader, had struck out the earlier permission and granted fresh permission on November 26.The bench issued a show-cause notice to Sabir, asking him to explain why he had altered the permission without the court's approval. Sabir accepted the notice and sought a week's time to respond.The court warned the office of the additional advocate general against retaining documents after showing them to the bench and obtaining permission to file them.Taking note of the SSP's submission that the two suspended personnel would not be reinstated until the departmental inquiry was completed, the court recorded his undertaking.The bench directed that a copy of its order be sent to the chief minister and chief secretary of Madhya Pradesh. The matter has been listed for further hearing on December 2.
Article Summary: Madhya Pradesh high court questions senior police officers over alleged suppression of facts and failure to act on official communications. Court accuses police hierarchy of attempting to shield those responsible for lapses. Case relates to a criminal appeal filed by Ramjeet alias Ramjilal and others.

Article Title: Diljit Dosanjh's Mumbai concert today: 500+ cops, bomb squads and no-car zone after threat email; MNS seeks ban on racecourse shows over drugs
Article Text:
Diljit Dosanjh's Mumbai concert under tight security today

500+ personnel, five entry gates and a no-car zone

MNS wants concerts at Mahalaxmi Racecourse, NSCI Dome stopped

Police step up anti-drug checks at concert venues

(With agency inputs)





MUMBAI: With more than 500 police personnel, bomb detection teams and a strict no-car zone, actor-singer Diljit Dosanjh's concert at Mahalaxmi Racecourse on Friday is taking place under heightened security after a threat email warned of possible attacks on the venue and Metro stations.But security is not the only controversy surrounding the show; the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) has demanded a ban on concerts at the racecourse and NSCI Dome, alleging that such events have become hubs for drug use and civic disruption.The threat email, received on Thursday, the anniversary of the 26/11 terror attacks, warned of blasts, grenade attacks and improvised explosive devices at the mayor's office, Metro stations and Dosanjh's concert.The sender identified herself as Hannah Meler and referred to Khalistan and the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, besides threatening violence linked to a programme involving the singer and people associated with the event.Following the threat, Mumbai Police have stepped up security at Mahalaxmi Racecourse, where Dosanjh is scheduled to perform as part of his RuPay AURA India Tour 2026.More than 500 police personnel will be deployed at the venue, including around 200 constables, 150 women constables and 75 officers, along with personnel in plain clothes stationed around the singer.Dog squads and an Anti-Narcotics Cell (ANC) team will also be present.Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad teams have swept the venue, while entry checks will be conducted at all five gates instead of the earlier three. Private security personnel have also been engaged to assist the police.A no-car zone extending 500 to 700 metres around the racecourse will be enforced, and parking will not be allowed at the event. No road diversions have been announced so far.Organisers have also been instructed not to disclose details of the singer's hotel or arrival time. Posters, banners, signs and flags of any kind have been barred inside the venue.Even as the city prepares for the concert, the MNS has written to Mumbai Police seeking an immediate and permanent ban on live music concerts and large-scale entertainment events at Mahalaxmi Racecourse and the NSCI Dome.The party has cited alleged drug use, traffic congestion and the death of a young man at a concert venue last year.In a letter to the police, MNS leader Dinesh Dnyaneshwar Punde claimed that drugs were openly sold and consumed at such events, putting young people at risk. He cited a November 22 event at which the ANC reportedly booked 12-13 people for drug consumption, and referred to an earlier fatal incident involving a young man.The letter also flagged traffic congestion caused by concerts, saying it created difficulties for local residents. Punde warned that MNS workers and residents would stage a road blockade if permissions for such events continued to be granted.The MNS demand comes amid increased scrutiny of drug use at large events. Earlier this week, Mumbai Police deployed a newly launched ANC forensic van outside Mahalaxmi Racecourse as part of efforts to curb narcotics use.The mobile unit is equipped with five rapid detection machines and 360-degree surveillance cameras. These include TruNarc, which uses Raman laser technology to identify narcotic substances without opening their packaging; Gemini, which can identify a wider range of substances, including narcotics, hazardous chemicals and explosives; and the Dräger DrugTest 5000, which detects drug consumption through oral swab testing.The police said the equipment would help personnel identify substances and detect drug consumption at event venues.
Article Summary: Diljit Dosanjh's concert at Mahalaxmi Racecourse on Friday is taking place under heightened security. A threat email warned of possible attacks on the venue and Metro stations. The Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) has demanded a ban on concerts at the racecourse and NSCI Dome.

Article Title: Nuh court awards 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment to 4 men in 11-year-old firing case
Article Text:
4 men were sentenced to 10 years in prison for attempted murder stemming from a family feud.





GURGAON: An attack allegedly driven by an old family feud and carried out with illegal firearms has landed four men in jail for 10 years each, with a Nuh court holding that the assault was premeditated and could have cost the victim his life.Additional sessions judge Sandeep Chauhan sentenced Naseem, Sameem, Irfan and Hanif to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment each in an attempt-to-murder case dating back nearly 11 years.The court also imposed a fine of Rs 25,000 on each convict, with an additional 10 months’ simple imprisonment if the fine is not paid.According to police, the four had attacked Fakruddin and his son Denu over an old rivalry stemming from the murder of Irfan’s brother. The accused allegedly planned the assault in advance and used illegally procured firearms to target the father-son duo.Fakruddin was fired upon during the attack but survived. Police registered a case, collected evidence and arrested the accused before filing the case for trial.During the proceedings, the court observed that the attack appeared to have been premeditated and that Fakruddin could have been killed had the assailants succeeded in carrying out their plan. The four were convicted and sentenced on the basis of the evidence presented during the trial.Another accused, Assam, was declared a proclaimed offender through an order dated Sept 17, police said.
Article Summary: Naseem, Sameem, Irfan and Hanif sentenced to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment each in an attempt-to-murder case dating back nearly 11 years. The court also imposed a fine of Rs 25,000 on each convict, with an additional 10 months’ simple imprisonment if the fine is not paid.

Article Title: 10-year-old sexually assaulted in Delhi park by repeat offender months after release from jail; follows Aastha Kunj gang rape case
Article Text:
A 10-year-old girl was sexually assaulted in a park in northwest Delhi (Representative image)





NEW DELHI: A 10-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted by a man inside a park in northwest Delhi on November 24. The accused was caught and thrashed by local residents before being handed over to the police.The accused, identified as Rajesh, a resident of northwest Delhi, was previously convicted in a 2018 case involving the sexual assault of a minor in Swaroop Nagar and sentenced to seven years in prison. He was released from jail a few months ago, police sources said.According to police, a PCR call regarding the incident was received around 11.30 am, following which a team from the local police station rushed to the spot.The initial inquiry revealed that the girl, a Class IV student, was inside the park when the accused allegedly approached her and attempted to sexually assault her.There were also claims that she was passing through the park on her way to a relative's house after school, which police have denied.Hearing the girl's screams, people in the vicinity rushed to help her, caught the accused and assaulted him before handing him over to the police.Police sources said the 35-year-old accused was unmarried and had allegedly been estranged from his family. Investigators are also probing whether he was under the influence of any intoxicating substance at the time of the incident. His blood samples have been sent for testing.His electronic devices are being seized and examined as part of the investigation, including to check his internet search history. Police will also investigate whether he was involved in similar incidents after his release from jail that may have gone unreported.The incident has also raised questions over security arrangements at the park. Police sources said the sprawling park had only one guard deployed at the time of the incident, despite requiring at least four to five personnel for effective monitoring."The park is quite large and requires at least four to five guards, but only one was present when the incident took place. We had earlier flagged the security concern with the concerned authorities and will pursue the matter further," a police source said.The incident comes two months after three men posing as policemen allegedly threatened and gang-raped a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park in southeast Delhi's Kalkaji.The girl told police that she visited Kalkaji Temple with her friend on her birthday, September 22, and later entered Aastha Kunj Park. The two were sitting near the swings when three men, aged between 30 and 35, allegedly approached them, slapped her friend and posed as policemen.When she resisted, one of the men allegedly threatened her by showing a gun. The trio then took out knives, led her to a secluded part of the park and allegedly sexually assaulted her.
Article Summary: A 10-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted by a man inside a park in northwest Delhi on November 24. The accused was caught and thrashed by local residents before being handed over to the police. Police sources said the sprawling park had only one guard deployed at the time of the incident.

Article Title: ‘Hardest meeting of my life’: Jensen Huang apologises to Nvidia staff after CEO comeback
Article Text:
Huang also sought to reassure women employees, describing himself as 'one of our greatest advocates for creating an environment for women.'

Huang says he is undergoing therapy

Nvidia CEO promises regular performance reviews

Huang rejects claims of preferential treatment

Why Huang stepped down and returned as Nvidia CEO

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologised to employees on Tuesday for violating the company's code of conduct and admitted making “very serious personal mistakes” during his first all-hands meeting since returning to the top post. Huang acknowledged that his personal behaviour had hurt his family and wife. He also promised to hold himself to higher standards and undergo regular performance reviews based on feedback from employees.“This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang said, according to a report by The Wired. “The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife.”Addressing employees, Huang said he had been attending therapy sessions every day for an hour and a half. He added that the sessions had been helping him.“I made some very serious personal mistakes. I hurt my family, I hurt my wife,” he said.Huang also stressed that Nvidia's code of conduct remained applicable to everyone in the company, including its top leadership. He said he had written much of the code himself and that it was designed to “create an environment that’s safe for people.”He warned that violations would not be tolerated. However, he clarified that every violation would not automatically lead to an employee's dismissal.“But that does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” he said. “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” would determine the action taken.Huang also addressed criticism of his intense management style and acknowledged that his behaviour had sometimes affected employees negatively.While he maintained that his demanding approach helped push people to perform better, he admitted that he sometimes went too far.“It disempowers them, and that’s not right,” Huang said.He said he needed to find a way to maintain his commitment to Nvidia without hurting the people working for him.“I need to hold myself to a higher standard at this time,” he said.Huang also announced that he would undergo a 360-degree performance review. The process would involve seeking feedback from people working with him, potentially as often as once a month.He said he would be the first and only person at Nvidia to undergo such a review and did not intend to introduce the practice across the company.The CEO also pushed back against suggestions that he had been reinstated because of his standing in the technology industry.“There are rumors on the internet that apparently I’m a tech bro, and therefore I’m back,” Huang said.He rejected the suggestion that his position gave him special treatment or placed him above Nvidia's code of conduct.Huang also sought to reassure women employees, describing himself as “one of our greatest advocates for creating an environment for women”.He highlighted the company's flexible work policies, saying they allowed employees to build their families while pursuing their careers.“If I did anything that put that in jeopardy, I cannot tell you how sad I am, and I’ll do everything I can to fix it,” he said.He further sought to reassure employees about the company's ability to function without him, saying his brief absence had demonstrated its operational strength.“I promise you, whether I’m here or not, this company is wired up to execute, execute, and execute,” Huang said.Nvidia's board accepted Huang's resignation earlier this month following concerns about his personal conduct and lack of candour. The development came after media reports about alleged extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman accused of having links to Chinese intelligence services.However, the same board reinstated him on Monday, just 11 days after accepting his resignation. The decision followed fresh assurances from Huang and information from the Trump administration that he was not under federal scrutiny.His return has drawn mixed reactions within Nvidia. While some employees welcomed the decision, others reportedly remain concerned about his conduct and the board's move to reinstate him.The controversy has also led to continued legal and regulatory scrutiny. Nvidia's board is investigating whether Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence. US lawmakers are also expecting him to testify before Congress next week.Meanwhile, lawsuits and other investigations are ongoing into the company's disclosures about Huang's conduct and its compliance with US export controls on chips.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang apologised to employees on Tuesday for violating the company's code of conduct. He admitted making'very serious personal mistakes' during his first all-hands meeting since returning to the top post. Huang acknowledged that his personal behaviour had hurt his family and wife. He also promised to hold himself to higher standards and undergo regular performance reviews based on feedback from employees.

Article Title: How Jensen Huang's Silicon Valley friends ran a 'war room' to get him back as Nvidia CEO
Article Text:
Marc Andreessen, Travis Kalanick, and Nvidia investors built a 'war room' to bring back Jensen Huang

Jensen Huang's allies began lobbying within hours of his resignation

A 45-minute call with JD Vance took Huang's case to the White House

Nvidia's board took Jensen Huang back after a secret Sunday meeting

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia's chief executive just 11 days after he resigned. The push that got him there started with a small circle of friends in Silicon Valley. Tech founders and investors set up what one of them called a "war room", lobbied Nvidia's board in public and in private, and then pulled in President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance , the Financial Times reported.Nvidia's board voted unanimously on November 23 to reinstate Huang. Six days earlier, board chair Harvey Jones had said the company did not intend to bring him back. Huang stepped down on November 12 after reports of two affairs. One was with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer. US officials believe she was a Chinese intelligence asset. The other was with a subordinate.Nvidia shares jumped more than 30% on Monday, the biggest one-day gain in market value on record for a US company, according to The Wall Street Journal.According to the FT, the group included Uber founder Travis Kalanick, investors Gavin Baker, Brad Gerstner and Marc Andreessen, and Goldman Sachs executive John Underwood. Within 24 hours, Baker and Gerstner, both large Nvidia shareholders, published an open letter asking the board to keep "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang".The effort had Huang's backing, the FT reported. Publicly, Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney threw their weight behind a "Bring Jensen Back" letter.A letter calling for his return gathered more than 200,000 signatures, the WSJ reported, and employees signing it warned of "irreplaceable talent loss".One of the allies arranged a 45-minute phone call between Huang and Vance last week. Huang used it to defend his views on US export controls, remote access to chips and his Megaspeed dealings, the FT said.Trump stepped in after returning from China at the end of last week. He asked Vance to talk to Huang and work with the board, The New York Times reported. Vance set out to get the board two things it needed: an assurance that the administration did not see Huang as a national security threat, and a statement that he was not facing criminal charges.The WSJ reported that Attorney General Todd Blanche told Trump and Vance on Saturday that Huang was not the target or subject of any Justice Department investigation. Over the next 48 hours, Trump, Vance and other officials relayed that to board members.Trump told the WSJ he reached the board "in numerous ways" and "through representatives", and that the falling stock made his job easier. "The climate became more and more right as the company stock began to tumble," he told the paper. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had earlier called for a leadership shake-up at Nvidia. He softened his stance over the weekend.The talks were so secretive that interim CEO Colette Kress was kept out, the FT reported. During a long board session on Sunday, Huang disclosed affairs beyond the two already reported and came across as sorry for them, according to the WSJ. After conversations about candour, the board decided his return was the best path.On Monday, Huang walked into Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters to cheering staff. "I'm terribly sorry for putting all of you through all of this," he said. At an all-hands meeting on Tuesday, he told employees he was in therapy for 90 minutes a day. He called the idea that Trump pressured the board "completely untrue", the NYT reported.Even after the rally, Nvidia is worth about a fifth less than it was a month ago, the FT noted. Nvidia and Huang still face FBI and SEC probes, plus congressional investigations. Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter have been summoned to hearings in Washington next week.The board says its internal investigation will continue and that Nvidia will hire a chief compliance officer. On Monday, the US Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang's allies began lobbying within hours of his resignation. A 45-minute call with JD Vance took Huang's case to the White House. Nvidia's board voted unanimously on November 23 to reinstate Huang. Huang stepped down on November 12 after reports of two affairs.

Article Title: Winter fog: Railways cancels 20 trains, reduces frequency of others
Article Text:
Representational image

Patna

:

:





The railways has decided to cancel at least 20 mail and express trains and reduce the frequency of several others from Dec 1 to Feb 28, 2027, as part of its safety measures during the fog-season.East Central Railway (ECR) chief public relations officer Saraswati Chandra said the decision was taken in view of anticipated dense fog in several northern parts of the country during the winter months.“Poor visibility caused by fog often affects train operations, resulting in delays, disruption of schedules and difficulties in maintaining punctuality. Thus, the precautionary measure is intended to ensure safe and smooth train operations during this period,” he said.Chnadra said the changes would affect several trains originating from, terminating at or passing through the ECR jurisdiction. While some trains would remain cancelled throughout the three-month period, the frequency of several others would be reduced from seven days a week to two or three days.Among the important trains to remain cancelled are the Muzaffarpur–Prayagraj Junction Express (14111/14112), Barauni–Ambala Harihar Express (14523/14524), Purnia Court–Amritsar Janseva Express (14617/14618), Gaya–Kamakhya Express (15619/15620) and Howrah–Dehradun Upasana Express (13035/13036).The frequency of several trains, including the Barauni–Gwalior Express, Bhagalpur–Anand Vihar Garib Rath, Patliputra–Lucknow Express, Patliputra–Gorakhpur Express, Sealdah–Ajmer Express and Kolkata–Amritsar Express, will also be reduced during this period.Passengers have been advised to check the latest status of their trains before starting their journeys and regularly visit the official Indian Railways website or authorised railway enquiry platforms for updates on cancellations, frequency changes and partial cancellations.The railways has also urged passengers to plan their journeys accordingly to avoid inconvenience during the fog season. The revised arrangements will remain in force until Feb 28, 2027.
Article Summary: The railways has decided to cancel at least 20 mail and express trains and reduce the frequency of several others from Dec 1 to Feb 28, 2027. The decision was taken in view of anticipated dense fog in several northern parts of the country during the winter months.

Article Title: 7 killed after vehicle falls into gorge in Uttarakhand
Article Text:
The accident occurred near Rikhnikhal's Kalwadi.





DEHRADUN: Seven women belonging to a self-help group and a driver were killed when their vehicle plunged into a gorge about 100 metres deep on the Rikhnikhal-Satpuli motor road near Kotdwar on Saturday.The women, residents of Kotnali Bhangalwan in Rikhnikhal block, were returning to their village after completing bank-related work in Siddhkhal when the vehicle went out of control near Kotdwar, killing all eight occupants, including the driver.Local villagers were the first to reach the spot and began rescue efforts. Officials from Rikhnikhal, Lansdowne and Kotdwar subsequently rushed to the site.Chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami expressed grief over the deaths and conveyed his condolences to the bereaved families. He directed the district administration to expedite relief and rescue operations.Lansdowne Sub-Divisional Magistrate Shalini Maurya also reached the site with her team. Villagers, police and revenue department personnel launched a joint operation to retrieve the bodies from the gorge.The CM also instructed officials to ensure medical care for the injured and arrange for those critically injured to be airlifted to advanced medical centres.
Article Summary: Seven women belonging to a self-help group and a driver were killed when their vehicle plunged into a gorge about 100 metres deep. The women were returning to their village after completing bank-related work in Siddhkhal. The vehicle went out of control near Kotdwar, killing all eight occupants, including the driver.

Article Title: UP Police constable found dead at home, wife arrested
Article Text: Bulandshahr: A 39-year-old UP Police constable was found dead at his home after returning from security duty at Ganga Mela in Hapur, with his brother alleging that he had been facing mental harassment over his wife’s alleged relationships with two men. Based on the complaint, police registered an FIR against his wife and three others for abetment of suicide. His wife was arrested and sent to judicial custody on Friday.The constable, a native of Phoolpur village, was posted at Maudarwaja police station in Farrukhabad district. He had joined the police department as a home guard in 2011 and was recruited as a constable in 2021.He was recently deployed for security duty at Ganga Mela in Garhmukteshwar and returned home on Nov 24 after completing his assignment. He lived with his wife and their two children, aged seven and nine, in Chandanpur Khadar village.According to police, he went to sleep as usual on Tuesday night, but family members found him unresponsive in bed the next morning. They alerted the police, who reached the spot, conducted inquest proceedings and sent the body for post-mortem examination.In his complaint, the constable’s brother alleged that his brother had been facing mental harassment over his wife’s alleged relationships with two men. He claimed that the issue had led to frequent arguments between the couple and that the constable was threatened whenever he objected. The complainant held the alleged harassment and domestic disputes responsible for his brother’s death.SHO Amit Tomar said, “Based on the complaint, Rahra police registered an FIR under BNS Section 108 (abetment of suicide) against the wife, the two men named, both residents of Chandanpur Khadar, and another man from Deva in Bachhrawan.”
Article Summary: 39-year-old UP Police constable was found dead at his home after returning from security duty at Ganga Mela in Hapur. His brother alleged that he had been facing mental harassment over his wife’s alleged relationships with two men. Based on the complaint, police registered an FIR against his wife and three others for abetment of suicide.

Article Title: Terror plot targeting Delhi-NCR foiled, 'Jaish operative' held
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





NEW DELHI: A major terror plot targeting Delhi-NCR was foiled following the covert capture of an alleged Jaish-e-Mohammed operative by intelligence agencies in the capital. Sources said Friday that the accused, an alleged radical ideologue operating under the shadow alias of 'Umar', was intercepted by agencies last month and handed over to Delhi's special cell.The arrest followed an investigation into the sophisticated digital networks run by the ISI-backed terror group to brainwash young recruits into carrying out local attacks. The suspect was accused of allegedly radicalising young recruits through social media platforms including Whatsapp, Telegram and Instagram, and motivating them to carry out an attack.Senior officials said that the operation was ongoing. It is unclear if the suspect was connected to the same module busted by Gujarat ATS Thursday.The arrest had led to the questioning of multiple suspects connected to the operative even as a manhunt was launched for the Pakistan-based handler. However, no further arrests were made as the suspects connected through chat platforms had not "breached a threshold", were in early stages of radicalisation and deserved a chance to be rehabilitated, sources added.The arrest came at a time when the agencies were on alert on the heels of the Red Fort blast anniversary.Inputs had suggested that many Pakistan-backed modules including that of Shehzad Bhatti were attempting to carry out a re-run of last year's incident which had led to around a dozen deaths.Officials said that the probe was focused on uncovering a wider network, including its funding, logistics and operational links. Investigators are also examining whether the arrested accused had planned or executed any specific acts of violence in the past.Cops are likely to file a chargesheet in the case in the coming weeks. To build a watertight case under Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) and sections of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), investigators will be using a comprehensive dossier of forensic digital evidence extracted from the accused's seized devices.
Article Summary: Alleged radical ideologue operating under the shadow alias of 'Umar' was intercepted by agencies last month and handed over to Delhi's special cell. The suspect was accused of allegedly radicalising young recruits through social media platforms including Whatsapp, Telegram and Instagram.

Article Title: 28-year-old killed as man throws gas cylinder from 3rd floor after parking argument in Delhi
Article Text:
Police cordon off a residential lane where a gas cylinder can be seen lying. (AI image)





NEW DELHI: A 28-year-old man was killed after a gas cylinder allegedly thrown from the third floor of a residential building struck him in southwest Delhi's Bindapur Extension on Friday evening.Around 7.15pm, Dabri police station received a PCR call reporting that a man had thrown a gas cylinder from the building's third floor and that the injured person had been taken to hospital. The victim was subsequently declared dead by hospital authorities.The deceased was identified as Sahil, a resident of the first floor of the same building who worked at a weekly market. He is survived by his 21-year-old wife, Ritu, their one-and-a-half-year-old son Kartik and his mother.The alleged accused has been identified as Shivam Sharma alias Shiv (24), who lives on the third floor of the building. Shivam works in tailoring and stitching at a factory in Bindapur, while his mother is employed as a freelancer with a company.According to preliminary information, the sequence of events began around 7pm when an argument reportedly broke out between Shivam and another occupant in the building's parking area.The disagreement allegedly escalated into a heated confrontation. Police said Shivam had been consuming alcohol since morning and had not attended work that day.Following the argument, Shivam allegedly went upstairs in anger and threw a gas cylinder from the third floor. It came crashing down and struck Sahil, who was present below.Police have registered a case and are examining CCTV footage from the area.
Article Summary: A 28-year-old man was killed after a gas cylinder allegedly thrown from the third floor of a residential building struck him. The deceased was identified as Sahil, a resident of the first floor of the same building who worked at a weekly market. The alleged accused has been identified as Shivam Sharma alias Shiv.

Article Title: When a child speaks up: DSLSA trains teachers on responding to abuse
Article Text:
This daylight view shows an elevated segment of the Delhi Metro infrastructure, featuring a Magenta Line train approaching along a curved concrete track structure on the left. On the right side, the elevated platform overlooks a busy ground-level road with vehicular traffic running parallel to a dense residential neighborhood filled with multi-story houses and trees. Another train passes along an intersecting lower elevated section below. (TOI Photo: Delhi News)





New Delhi: A child growing unusually quiet, an otherwise regular student missing school, or someone confiding in a teacher about online abuse or sexual assault — recognising the signs is often only half the challenge. For Deepti Arora, an Education, Vocational Guidance and Counselling (EVGC) counsellor at a west Delhi school for 12 years, the bigger question has been what to do next: whom to report to, when to involve the police and how to initiate the process.These questions were at the heart of a training programme organised by Delhi State Legal Services Authority (DSLSA) Friday, where around 146 teachers-in-charge from schools across five district legal services authorities were familiarised with child protection procedures, reporting mechanisms and access to legal aid under Surakshit Bachpan Abhiyan and the NALSA (Child-Friendly Legal Services for Children) Scheme, 2024.The programme marks the campaign’s second phase, focused on equipping teachers to respond to abuse disclosures and connect children with legal aid. The first phase involved school outreach to sensitise staff on child protection.“We are trying to create a support system within schools so that children can approach teachers and counsellors themselves, knowing there is someone they can turn to and that their concerns will be addressed in their familiar setting,” said Judge Sunena Sharma, member secretary, DSLSA, explaining the objective of the programme.Across four sessions, teachers were familiarised with legal aid resources, coordination mechanisms and child protection laws. In one session, judicial officers Sheetal Chaudhary Pradhan and Deepali Srivastava, among others, stressed the need for “immediate intervention”, explaining reporting procedures and access to free legal aid through Delhi’s 12 district legal services authorities.For Arora and several other participants, however, acting promptly often meant navigating layers of authority within schools, leaving them unsure of whom to approach and how to initiate a complaint. “I would always feel I had to report such incidents to my principal first. Fortunately, my principal has been supportive and helped take complaints forward so the police could begin an investigation. But not every teacher may have that support. Knowing now that we can approach the district cells directly and reach out through helpline numbers has taken away that doubt,” she said.The uncertainty, participants said, was compounded by the stigma surrounding child sexual abuse cases and apprehensions about getting drawn into lengthy legal proceedings. Dr Manju, another participant, said the complexity of legal procedures often made teachers hesitant to intervene.“Teachers, like anyone else, associate ‘court kachehri’ with endless complications. There is a hesitation about getting involved, especially when you are unsure how much you can help. Although laws such as the POCSO Act and other child protection measures are strictly followed, simplifying this for us, makes it less intimidating,” she said.One such session also focused on recognising warning signs and making children feel safe enough to speak. Participant Shweta Chaudhary flagged the dilemma teachers often face in assessing whether a complaint is “genuine”. Addressing this, Bharati Ali, board director of Help for Children in Need Foundation, said, “Speaking to a child in a comfortable setting can help them open up. If suspicions persist, teachers can approach the DLSA counsellor, who can speak to the child and, if necessary, involve the parents while maintaining confidentiality. ”
Article Summary: Around 146 teachers-in-charge from schools across five district legal services authorities were familiarised with child protection procedures. The programme marks the campaign’s second phase, focused on equipping teachers to respond to abuse disclosures and connect children with legal aid. The first phase involved school outreach to sensitise staff on child protection.

Article Title: A Baltimore lawsuit says social workers routinely remove children without judges' approval, affecting more than 400 children a year; one couple says their two youngsters have been separated for nearly
Article Text:
Baltimore parents and children filed a class-action lawsuit challenging BCDSS’s unconstitutional child removal. (Representative Image)

The Washington Post

Couple's children remain in state custody nearly two years after removal

Lawsuit alleges poverty-related concerns lead to family separations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A group of Baltimore parents and children has filed a federal class-action lawsuit against the city's social services department, alleging that officials routinely remove children from their families without obtaining prior approval from a judge, even when there is no emergency, according toThe lawsuit claims that the Baltimore City Department of Social Services (BCDSS) separates more than 400 children from their families every year through a process that violates their constitutional rights.The plaintiffs allege that families are often kept apart for weeks or months without a meaningful opportunity to challenge the removals. They are seeking court intervention to stop the alleged practices, along with compensation for the harm caused by the separations.According to the complaint, the practice disproportionately affects Black families, with officials allegedly treating conditions linked to poverty as evidence of child neglect.The lawsuit was brought on behalf of two Baltimore families who say they experienced the department's alleged practices firsthand.One couple, Candace and Edward Lovett, said social workers and police arrived at their home in February 2025 and took their 19-month-old child without a court order, citing concerns about the child's well-being.The child was initially placed with a relative. Four weeks later, the department took both their children into state custody, again without prior judicial approval, the lawsuit alleges.The couple's children have remained in state custody for more than 19 months, despite their efforts to have them returned, according to the complaint.Edward Lovett described the separation as deeply painful, saying he missed his children and that barely being able to see them had caused immense emotional distress.His wife is now pregnant, and the couple fears that authorities could also take their newborn after birth.Two plaintiffs in the lawsuit are pregnant and due to give birth in the coming weeks. They are seeking emergency court protection to prevent the department from taking their babies without following due process.The complaint alleges that many children are removed following reports of neglect linked to poverty rather than allegations of serious physical or sexual abuse.Housing instability, poor living conditions, parental co-sleeping with children and a lack of basic resources are among the concerns cited in the lawsuit.The plaintiffs argue that families could instead receive support such as housing assistance, financial aid, utility support and basic supplies, without having their children taken away.The lawsuit claims the department routinely removes children without establishing whether an emergency exists that would justify bypassing judicial approval.It alleges violations of the Fourth and Fourteenth Amendments to the US Constitution and provisions of the Maryland Declaration of Rights. The plaintiffs are seeking changes that would require notice and a court hearing before a child is removed, except in genuine emergencies.The Maryland Department of Human Services, which oversees the city's social services department, declined to comment on the pending litigation. The Maryland Judiciary also declined to comment, citing rules that prevent judges from discussing specific cases.The case comes amid wider efforts by parental rights advocates to challenge child removal practices across the US. Similar lawsuits have also been filed in New York and Georgia.
Article Summary: Lawsuit alleges poverty-related concerns lead to family separations. Baltimore City Department of Social Services (BCDSS) separates more than 400 children from their families every year through a process that violates their constitutional rights. Plaintiffs allege that families are often kept apart for weeks or months without a meaningful opportunity to challenge the removals.

Article Title: Deepam lit on deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai amid tight security following Supreme Court order
Article Text:
The lighting followed a fresh direction issued by the Supreme Court on Friday. (Photo by K Antony Xavier)





MADURAI: A deepam was lit on the deepathoon atop the Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai on Saturday, four days after it remained unlit at the spot despite an earlier Supreme Court order permitting lighting of it.The lighting followed a fresh direction issued by the Supreme Court on Friday. The court appointed retired Madras high court judges Justice S Vaidyanathan and Justice V Parthiban as receivers of the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple and entrusted them with ensuring compliance with its direction. Security of the temple and the entire hill was handed over to the Central Reserve Police Force ( CRPF ).The controversy intensified after the court's Nov 20 interim order permitting the Karthigai Deepam to be lit on the deepathoon on Nov 24 as a one-time arrangement. The court had then made the Madurai district collector responsible for coordinating the arrangements.However, on Tuesday, the festival day, the lamp was lit around 6pm at the customary deepa mandapam near the Uchi Pillayar Temple, while the deepathoon remained unlit. Hindu outfits protested it, and police detained several members amid heightened security.Hearing contempt petitions on Friday, the Supreme Court took exception to the non-implementation of its earlier order, suspended the temple's board of trustees and issued contempt notices to senior state officials.It directed the receivers to ensure the deepam was lit at the deepathoon situated near the Sikandar Badusha Dargah on Saturday, bringing the court-ordered ceremony to fruition.Earlier, in a press release, the receivers of the Arulmigu Subramania Swamy Temple said in view of public safety, the sanctity of the hill and law and order maintenance, elaborate security arrangements had been put in place. Entry to the hill was strictly restricted to temple staffers, security personnel and a select group of 50 devotees with prior permission, who would be allowed to ascend between 2.30pm and 3pm.Receivers appealed to devotees and the public to respect the apex court's order, adhere to instructions from the administration and security forces, and extend full cooperation to maintain peace.
Article Summary: A deepam was lit on the deepathoon atop the Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai on Saturday. The lighting followed a fresh direction issued by the Supreme Court on Friday. Security of the temple and the entire hill was handed over to the Central Reserve Police Force.
